01Chapter 1 · Introduction to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

Introduction — RAG kya hai aur kyun zaroori hai

Ek AI engineer apni company ke liye ek internal support chatbot banati hai — ek off-the-shelf large language model (LLM) se ek afternoon me prototype taiyaar ho jata hai. Model fluent baat karta hai, lambe documents summarize kar deta hai, code bhi likh deta hai. Lekin jaise hi usse company ke apne systems ke baare me poocha jata hai — "January ke baad refund policy kya hogi?" ya "is hafte kaunse customer accounts follow-up ke liye flagged hain?" — jawab bikhar jate hain. Model confident tareeke se aisi baatein bol deta hai jo company ke asal data se koi connection nahi rakhti. Kabhi outdated policy bata deta hai, kabhi poori tarah bekaar jawab. Problem model ki fluency nahi hai — problem uski blindness hai.

LLM ki sabse badi limitation — training ke bahar ka gyaan

Advanced se advanced LLM bhi sirf us data par train hota hai jo training ke waqt available tha — books, articles, code repositories, public web content. Isse use language ki broad, generalized samajh milti hai, aur woh aise tasks bhi kar leta hai jin par use explicitly train nahi kiya gaya tha. Lekin training dataset kitna bhi bada kyun na ho, usme company ke private documents, internal knowledge base, ya pichhle hafte hue niche library ke updates kabhi nahi ho sakte. Isliye jab bhi task ko training window ke bahar ki information chahiye hoti hai, LLM eloquent lekin galat jawab de deta hai. Ye errors aksar hallucination ke roop me dikhte hain — fluent aur confident generated content jo kisi bhi asal data se supported nahi hota.

Training data badhana solution nahi hai

Duniya ki information — public, private, structured, unstructured, stable aur constantly changing — ko capture karke, clean karke ek hi training run me daalna possible nahi hai. Training khatm hote hi koi bhi model incomplete aur thoda outdated ho jata hai. Isliye retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) aaya: static model se "sab kuch jaanne" ki ummeed karne ke bajaye, RAG use dynamically woh relevant facts pull karne deta hai jo uske paas nahi hain. Support chatbot me RAG add karne par model user ke sawaal ke moment par exact wiki page, policy document ya support ticket history fetch kar sakta hai, aur phir apni generative capability se un retrieved materials par grounded final answer synthesize kar sakta hai. Result ek aisa system hai jo zyada accurate, zyada reliable aur hallucination ke liye bahut kam prone hai — kyunki uske paas aakhirkaar woh information hai jo use chahiye thi.

Closed-book test vs open-book test

Pure LLM use aur RAG ke beech ka farq bilkul closed-book test aur open-book test ke beech ke farq jaisa hai. Closed-book test me students ko sirf apni memory aur understanding par bharosa karna padta hai — koi textbook, notes ya reference material allowed nahi hota. Waise hi pure LLM usage me saari information sirf training ke dauraan include kiye gaye dataset par based hoti hai. Aisa knowledge LLM ke parameters (weights) me store hota hai — ek artificial neural network jiska behavior uske weights ki values se determine hota hai — aur ise parametric knowledge kehte hain. Open-book test me students exam ke dauraan textbooks ya notes consult kar sakte hain. RAG bilkul waise hi kaam karta hai — retrieval step real time me LLM ko additional information provide karta hai.

Is book ka focus

Ye book usi transformation par focus karti hai — LLMs jo sirf apni pre-training par bharosa karte hain, unse aise systems tak jo private, domain-specific aur constantly updated data par retrieval ke through reason kar sakte hain. RAG sirf ek technical enhancement nahi hai; ye generative AI ko real applications me genuinely useful banane ki chaabi hai. Aage ke chapters me aap seekhenge ki RAG stack ke har component — parsing, chunking, embedding, vector search, generation — kaise kaam karta hai, aur production me use scale karne ke liye kya chahiye.

Yaad rakho: LLM ki problem fluency nahi, blindness hai. Training data kabhi bhi aapka private, fresh data contain nahi kar sakta — isliye RAG model ko "sab kuch yaad rakhne" ke bajaye "sahi waqt par sahi fact dhoondh kar laane" ki capability deta hai.
SOURCESource: Hands-On RAG for Production, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Introduction to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

01.1Chapter 1 · Introduction to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

How Does RAG Work? — Retrieval + Generation

RAG query me do steps hote hain — R (retrieval) aur G (generation). Jab user RAG system ko query deta hai, pehle "R" step kick in karta hai aur query ke liye sabse relevant information retrieve karta hai. Uske baad "G" step aata hai, jahan ek large language model retrieved information aur query ko analyze karke retrieved facts par grounded ek proper response craft karta hai. "Augmented" shabd ka matlab hai ki retrieved information LLM ke prompt me add ki jati hai, aur is tarah uske internal knowledge ko additional facts se augment kiya jata hai.

Ek simple example — medical questions

Maan lo aap ek RAG chatbot bana rahe hain jo medical questions ke jawab deta hai, aur woh private data source par grounded hai jisme medical books aur journal papers hain. Query hai: "diabetes ke effective treatments kya hain?" Pehle retrieval step me system private data search karke diabetes ke treatment ke baare me relevant passages retrieve karta hai. Phir generation step me LLM ko original query aur retrieved facts milte hain, aur woh sirf is retrieved information ka use karke answer synthesize karta hai.

Basic RAG prompt structure

Ek bahut basic RAG prompt kuch is tarah dikhta hai: assistant ko question-answering task diya jata hai — retrieved context ke pieces use karke question ka jawab do, aur agar jawab nahi pata to bas keh do ki nahi pata. Prompt me question ki jagah asal question string aur context ki jagah facts ki list aati hai. Is tarah LLM ko task diya jata hai ki retrieved facts ko dekh kar query ka jawab usi information se de.

Blueprint of a RAG stack — do flows

RAG stack me do main flows hote hain — ingestion flow aur query flow. Ingestion flow data ko uske source (jaise database, S3 par PDF files ka set, Notion par text) se extract karke RAG stack me index karta hai. Query flow user query ka full processing karta hai — sahi facts retrieve karta hai aur LLM se generation karwata hai, jisse end user ko response milta hai.

Ingestion flow — data ko searchable banana

Data ingestion ke dauraan RAG system pehle input data ko multiple formats me convert karta hai jo query matching ke liye efficient aur effective hon — jinme sabse important hain vector embeddings, jo text ke semantic meaning ko represent karte hain. Vector embeddings ko phir ek special database me store kiya jata hai jise vector database (vector DB) kehte hain. Har vector ke saath asal text bhi store kiya jata hai, kyunki query-time processing me uski zaroorat padti hai. Data ko vectors me convert karne wale step ko aksar indexing ya embedding kehte hain. Production ingestion pipelines kaafi complex ho sakti hain — document pre-processing, chunking, embedding, data validation, multimodal inputs ka processing aur incremental updates jaise challenges aate hain.

Index, dataset aur corpus — teeno shabd

RAG ki duniya me index, dataset aur corpus shabd kuch had tak interchangeably use hote hain, aur teeno ingested data ko refer karte hain. Precise hona ho to: dataset (ya document set) woh initial raw collection hai jin source files se aap shuru karte hain; corpus woh curated, cleaned aur organized body of content hai; aur index woh high-performance data structure hai jo corpus se bana hai aur fast search aur retrieval ke liye optimized hai.

Query flow — retrieval phir generation

Query flow do operations karta hai — retrieval aur generation. Retrieval user query ko embedding vector me convert karke shuru hota hai, aur phir vector DB query embedding aur vector DB ke saare possible matching text (facts) ke beech similarity search karta hai. Embeddings se information dhoondhne ko semantic search kehte hain — embedding vector space me similarity search lagakar queries ke intent ko relevant text documents se semantically match kiya jata hai. Semantic search retrieval ka ek basic form hai, aur production deployments me high-quality RAG responses ke liye aksar kaafi nahi hota. Dusra basic form hai lexical search, jo texts ko unke likhe hue form ki similarity ke basis par match karta hai. Common hai advanced techniques use karna jaise hybrid search (semantic + lexical ka combination) ya reranking. Ideally retrieved text pieces me woh facts hon jo user query ka jawab dene ke liye highly relevant hon.

Generation aur citations

Relevant facts milne ke baad generation step ek dedicated prompt template craft karta hai jo LLM ko instruct karta hai ki retrieved results ki information use karke user query ka response kaise produce kare. Achhe RAG pipelines aksar LLM ko references ya citations produce karne ke liye bhi instruct karte hain, taaki response me sirf answer ka raw text na ho, balki ye bhi pata chale ki woh knowledge kis source par grounded hai.

Guardrails — response ke baad bhi ek step

LLM response bhej de, uske baad bhi kaam khatm nahi hota. Ek typical RAG query flow guardrails apply karta hai taaki response quality ke expected bar ko meet kare. Sabse pehle hai hallucination detection — validate karna ki LLM ne asal me diye gaye facts ka use karke aisa response banaya hai jo facts ke saath consistent hai, matlab usne kuch banaya to nahi. Additional guardrails me bias, toxic ya harmful responses, ya otherwise disallowed content ki detection aati hai.

Production me aur kya sochna padta hai

Pehle proof of concept se aage badh kar mission-critical production deployment me cheezein complex ho jati hain. Kuch sawaal jo uthte hain:

  • Response quality optimize kaise karein — sirf vector search se nahi, hybrid search, reranking ya aur advanced retrieval techniques se?
  • Tables, images, flowcharts aur dusre multimodal data ko high accuracy maintain karte hue RAG pipeline me kaise incorporate karein?
  • Quality measure kaise karein — retrieval, generation, hallucination aur citations — sirf pehli deployment par nahi, balki continuously, jab aap pipeline ko upgrade aur improve karte rahen?
  • Knowledge graphs ya agentic workflows me RAG ko kaise extend karein?

DevOps / MLOps / LLMOps — production ki reedh

Production scale par RAG pipeline design aur implement karne ke liye DevOps best practices (LLM ke naye era me jinhe aksar MLOps ya LLMOps kehte hain) ka robust set chahiye, taaki low latency, high availability aur strong security ensure ho:

  • CI/CD for RAG: automated data refresh — event-driven ETL processes jo source data update hote hi document ingestion updates (chunking, embedding aur indexing) automatically trigger karte hain; automated evaluation — RAG evaluation ko CI/CD pipeline me integrate karna, taaki koi naya model, prompt ya data change deploy na ho jo response quality degrade kare.
  • Prompt aur model controls: prompts ko code ki tarah version-controlled artifacts treat karna, aur saare components (embedding model, chunking logic, LLM) ko version karna, taaki reproducibility aur safe rollbacks possible hon.
  • Observability aur monitoring: ek single request ko pipeline se guzarte hue trace karna taaki "bad" responses debug ho sakein; har component ki performance aur cost track karna — ingestion, retrieval, LLM generation (token usage) aur overall cost per query.
  • Performance aur scalability: database optimization — efficient indexing strategies, sharding ya caching (vector DB, graph database, lexicon); optimized inference — embedding, reranking aur generation ke LLMs ke liye dedicated, auto-scaling inference endpoints.
  • Security aur governance: data-centric access control — granular, role-based access controls (RBAC) data level par, taaki pipeline sirf wahi documents retrieve aur present kare jinhe dekhne ke liye specific user authorized hai; encryption at rest aur in motion — saare data stores aur API communications ko strong cryptographic standards se encrypt karna; prompt aur output sanitization — prompt injection attacks mitigate karne ke liye strict input validation aur user tak pahunchne se pehle PII ya sensitive data scan karke redact karne ke liye output filtering.
Yaad rakho: RAG sirf "retrieve karo, phir generate karo" nahi hai. Ingestion flow data ko searchable banata hai, query flow retrieve + generate + guardrails karta hai, aur production me iske upar CI/CD, observability aur security ki poori layer chahiye hoti hai.
sample-rag.ipynb — Simple RAG Example with LangChain — GitHub: ofermend/hands-on-rag, chapter1/sample-rag.ipynb (https://github.com/ofermend/hands-on-rag/blob/main/chapter1/sample-rag.ipynb)
from langchain_community.document_loaders import PyPDFLoader
from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
from langchain_openai import OpenAIEmbeddings, ChatOpenAI
from langchain_community.vectorstores import LanceDB
from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate
from langchain_core.output_parsers import StrOutputParser
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnablePassthrough

# Load the PDF from URL
pdf_url = "https://www.adobe.com/be_en/active-use/pdf/Alice_in_Wonderland.pdf"
loader = PyPDFLoader(pdf_url)
pages = loader.load()

print(f"Loaded {len(pages)} pages from the PDF")

# Split documents into chunks
text_splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
    chunk_size=1000,
    chunk_overlap=200,
    length_function=len,
)

chunks = text_splitter.split_documents(pages)
print(f"Split into {len(chunks)} chunks")

# Create embeddings and vector store
embeddings = OpenAIEmbeddings(model="text-embedding-3-small")
vectorstore = LanceDB.from_documents(chunks, embeddings)

print(f"Created vector store with {len(chunks)} documents")

# Create the RAG chain using LCEL (LangChain Expression Language)
llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini", temperature=0)
retriever = vectorstore.as_retriever(search_kwargs={"k": 3})

def format_docs(docs):
    return "\n\n".join(doc.page_content for doc in docs)

prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(
    """Answer the question based only on the following context:

{context}

Question: {question}"""
)

rag_chain = (
    {"context": retriever | format_docs, "question": RunnablePassthrough()}
    | prompt
    | llm
    | StrOutputParser()
)

# Ask questions about Alice in Wonderland
questions = [
    "Who is the main character and what happens at the beginning of the story?",
    "What did the Caterpillar ask Alice?",
    "Describe the Mad Hatter's tea party.",
    "What happened at the trial at the end of the story?"
]

for q in questions:
    answer = rag_chain.invoke(q)
    print(f"Q: {q}")
    print(f"A: {answer}")
    print("-" * 60)
SOURCESource: Hands-On RAG for Production, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Introduction to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

01.2Chapter 1 · Introduction to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

RAG Versus Other Approaches — Chat with PDF, Fine-Tuning

LLM aur RAG ki duniya me pehli baar aane par kuch approaches RAG jaisi lagti hain — kam se kam function me — lekin unme aksar significant downsides hote hain, ya woh real-world, production-scale use cases support karne ke liye bahut simplistic hoti hain. Do sabse common alternatives hain "chat with PDF" aur fine-tuning.

RAG versus "Chat with PDF"

Aapko lag sakta hai ki RAG "chat with PDF" jaisa hai — aisi applications ki category jo user queries ke jawab documents ke set ke basis par deti hain. "Chat with PDF" application ko RAG se implement karna bilkul possible hai, lekin zyadaatar "chat with PDF" applications ek simple (lekin non-scalable) approach use karti hain: woh PDF file ka full text LLM prompt me daal deti hain, uske baad questions. Ye approach chhoti PDF files ke liye kaam karti hai, kyunki modern LLMs ab 256K ya 1M tokens tak ki context length support karte hain — aap shayad dasiyon ya saikadon PDF files bhi itni badi context window me fit kar lein. Lekin ye enterprise applications par scale nahi karti, jahan aksar hundreds of thousands documents hote hain, aur bahut badi context window bhi kaafi nahi hogi.

"Chat with PDF" ki teen limitations

  • Cost: LLMs chalana mehenga hota hai. Saare documents LLM ko feed karke aap query se irrelevant information bhi LLM ko feed karte hain — jo waste hai. RAG selectively sirf relevant information LLM ko feed karta hai, jisse ye cheaper, faster aur kisi bhi size par scalable hota hai.
  • Latency: Jo LLMs lambi sequence lengths process kar sakte hain, unhe bhi process karne me waqt lag sakta hai, jisse high latencies aur frustrating user experience milta hai.
  • Document selection: Enterprise application me maan lo aapko Google Drive, Notion, SharePoint aur S3 par PDF files ke set me maujood documents par grounded jawab chahiye. "Chat with PDF" me kisi ko phir bhi identify karna padega ki kaunse documents relevant hain aur unhe LLM ko feed karna padega. Ab hum wapas retrieval par aa gaye — aur ye bilkul RAG jaisa dikhne lagta hai.

RAG versus fine-tuning

Proprietary data ke saath LLM use karne wale developers aksar fine-tuning par consider karte hain — model ko apne specific domain ke hisaab se adapt karne ke liye. Is process me ek general-purpose pre-trained LLM liya jata hai aur private data par uski training "continue" ki jati hai. Ye additional training, jo typically kuch epochs chalti hai, model ke internal parameters adjust karti hai, uske knowledge, terminology aur response style ko naye data ke hisaab se specialize karti hai. Lekin fine-tuning me kai challenges hain.

Expertise gap

Fine-tuning sabse pehle ek mushkil kaam hai, jiske liye data ki careful preparation aur deep learning me gehri expertise chahiye, taaki overfitting, LLM ki general competencies me regression, naye data me maujood biases ko inadvertently model me introduce karna, ya AI safety risks jaise issues se bacha ja sake. Zyadaatar modern LLMs initial large-scale pre-training ke baad continued training se guzarte hain — supervised fine-tuning (SFT) aur reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF) jaisi techniques ke saath — aur frontier lab ke researchers model ko saare tasks me balance karne ki koshish karte hain. Is tarah ki fine-tuning in post-training regimes ko reverse ya interfere kar sakti hai, aur agar bahut care na li jaye to kai dimensions me regressions la sakti hai. Aur agar aapke paas required expertise wali team hai bhi, to bhi aapka data effective fine-tuning ke liye kaafi bada ya kaafi clean nahi bhi ho sakta.

Fine-tuning ki cost

Expertise gap ke alawa, fine-tuning kaafi mehengi hoti hai (GPU cost ke terms me), aur aapko khud se poochna chahiye: mujhe kitni baar fine-tune karna padega? Agar aapka dataset static hai, to zyada issue nahi hai — ek baar fine-tune karo aur ho gaya. Lekin zyadaatar real-world enterprise use cases me data frequently update hota hai — kya aap har din fine-tune karenge? Hafte me ek baar? Ye cost-effective solution hone ki sambhavna kam hai.

Access controls aur permissions — sabse overlooked point

Fine-tuning ke khilaf ek aksar overlooked, lekin bahut important, point access controls ka hai. Maan lo aapke dataset me multiple departments ke documents hain — engineering, HR, finance aur legal. Agar aap fine-tuning use karte hain, to aap effectively saara data model weights me incorporate kar dete hain. Ab agar company ka ek employee sawaal poochta hai aur fine-tuned LLM aisi confidential information ke basis par respond karta hai jo sirf CEO ya HR department ko available honi chahiye thi — to kya hoga? Fine-tuning me information ek single "blob" hoti hai, aur aap un documents ko alag nahi kar sakte jo CEO ko visible hone chahiye unse jo saare employees ko globally visible hain. Book isey Borg effect kehti hai — jaise ek mashhoor sci-fi series me Borg beings, cultures aur technology ko Collective me assimilate ya integrate kar lete hain, waise hi fine-tuning saara knowledge jise woh train karta hai, model weights me integrate kar deti hai, jisse data segmentation aur access control maintain karna mushkil ho jata hai. Isse departments ke beech sensitive data ka unintended exposure ho sakta hai, aur ye zyadaatar enterprises ke liye ek security concern hai.

Beshak, aap alag-alag user groups ya departments ke accessible data se alag LLMs fine-tune karne par consider kar sakte hain. Lekin isse multiple LLMs fine-tune hone lagenge — aur har ek ko alag se host karna padega. Ye resource-intensive hai aur queries ki routing chahiye hoti hai taaki har case ke liye intended model access ho. Overall, ye approach scalable nahi hai, aur cost aur complexity jaldi badh jati hai. Iske contrast me, RAG me aap retrieval step ke andar hi access controls aasani se implement kar sakte hain — data store me permission-based metadata fields add karke aur query time par filtering use karke.

Kya dono ko combine kar sakte hain?

Kuch bhi aapko fine-tuned LLM ko apne RAG stack ke hisse ke roop me use karne se nahi rokta. Agar aapke paas bahut saara internal data hai, aapko lagta hai ki fine-tuning se significant gains milenge, aur aapki team ke paas apne data par LLM ko properly fine-tune karne aur use apne RAG pipeline me host karne ki expertise hai — to aap standard LLM ke bajaye us fine-tuned LLM ko RAG ke generative step me use kar sakte hain. Summary me, "chat with PDF" aur fine-tuning kuch cases me valid approaches hain, lekin enterprise deployments ki baat aane par unki significant limitations hain.

Yaad rakho: "Chat with PDF" poora document prompt me daalta hai — mehenga, slow aur non-scalable. Fine-tuning knowledge ko weights me "pighla" deta hai — update karna mehenga hai aur access control lagbhag impossible ho jata hai. RAG dono problems se bachta hai kyunki knowledge bahar, searchable aur filterable rehta hai.

01.3Chapter 1 · Introduction to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

Key Benefits of RAG

RAG ki dusre approaches se comparison samajhne ke baad, ab RAG ke main benefits ko detail me dekhte hain — wahi benefits jo use mission-critical aur large-scale enterprise applications ke liye ek great approach banate hain.

RAG scalable aur efficient hai

RAG generative AI applications ko private datasets me ground karne ka ek efficient approach hai jo hundreds of thousands, millions, ya usse bhi zyada documents tak aasani se scale karta hai. Ye isliye possible hai kyunki RAG ke core me retrieval engine hai. Search ek hard problem hai jise decades se research kiya gaya hai, aur RAG me use karne ke liye ample approaches available hain. Search (aur is tarah RAG) documents ki sankhya ke saath scale karne ka rasta deta hai — jo ek LLM akele kabhi nahi kar sakta, kyunki uska self-attention mechanism apni sequence length ke saath quadratically scale karta hai. Dhyaan rahe, jabki retrieval algorithm khud efficiently scale kar sakta hai (modern indexing ke saath aksar sublinearly), production me overall system ki real-world scalability aksar engineering bottlenecks se dictate hoti hai — jaise database concurrency ya network latency.

RAG hallucinations kam karne me madad karta hai

Hallucination woh scenario hai jab LLM aisa content generate karta hai jo na uske apne world knowledge se supported hai, na prompt me feed ki gayi information se. RAG design se hi hallucinations kam karne me madad karta hai, closed-book tareeke se LLM se poochne ke comparison me. Reason ye hai: kyunki hum LLM ko source dataset se retrieved facts ka set dete hain jo user query ke liye relevant hain, to woh (agar properly build kiya gaya ho to) un facts ka use karke ek achha jawab dega. Jab relevant facts available nahi hote, to zyadaatar RAG applications ko instruct kiya jata hai ki woh bas "I don't know" respond karein. Iske contrast me, ek LLM lagbhag hamesha apne training set ke basis par kuch na kuch response dega, aur agar uske paas woh information nahi hai, to kai cases me woh kuch bana lega.

RAG explainability enable karta hai

RAG retrieved information use karke user queries ke jawab deta hai, isliye ek common practice hai ki RAG pipeline se generate ki gayi har sentence ke end me citations (jaise "[3,5]") implement ki jayein, agar aisa karne ko kaha jaye. Ye citations user trust badhati hain, kyunki users claims ko verify kar sakte hain, aur ye unhe hallucinations (jab model ne kuch bana liya) aur bad data (jab retrieved document me hi galat information thi) ke beech discriminate karne me bhi madad karti hain. Ek LLM ko proper prompts ke through ye bhi instruct kiya ja sakta hai ki woh retrieved information ko process karke aur us par reason karke explain kare ki woh jawab tak kaise pahuncha. Aisi high explainability tab unmatchable hoti hai jab ek LLM sirf apne parametric knowledge (training set se extract kiya gaya) se questions ke jawab deta hai, kyunki neural network weights se source ko reconstruct karna lagbhag impossible hota hai.

Knowledge ka near-instant addition aur removal

RAG me LLM se generated response ki quality retrieved data ki quality aur relevance par depend karti hai. Kyunki ye retrieved data LLM se bahar ek external system me store hota hai, use traditional ETL methods se trivially update kiya ja sakta hai — matlab LLM ke liye accessible knowledge ko regular basis par aasani se update kiya ja sakta hai. LLM ko diye gaye knowledge ki koi memory nahi hoti; use sirf query time par sahi facts retrieve karke dene hote hain. Iske comparison me, ek frontier model ya fine-tuned model me naya data integrate karne ya existing data remove/update karne ke liye retraining chahiye hoti hai — jo practice me lagbhag impossible hai (halanki machine unlearning par kuch academic research hai jo future me is challenge ko address karne me madad kar sakti hai).

Access controls aur security

RAG me aap access controls implement kar sakte hain — ingestion ke dauraan documents me permission information (metadata ke roop me) add karke, taaki query flow ko direct kiya ja sake ki woh permissions ke basis par kuch documents include kare ya exclude kare. Access controls ko properly support karna aksar RAG ki enterprise application me ek critical requirement hota hai, taaki aisa data leak na ho jo user dekhne ke liye authorized nahi hai. RAG aisi capabilities deta hai jo enterprise applications ke liye bahut attractive hain — khaas taur par un organizations ke liye jinhe strict access controls aur strong security chahiye, aur sabse important, jinhe response quality aur reduced hallucinations ki parwah hai.

Yaad rakho: RAG ke paanch bade fayde yaad rakho — scale, kam hallucination, citations se explainability, knowledge ka instant update, aur metadata-based access control. Ye paanchon milkar use enterprise ke liye fit banate hain.
SOURCESource: Hands-On RAG for Production, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Introduction to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
← Previous01.2 · RAG Versus Other Approaches — Chat with PDF, Fine-Tuning→ Next01.4 · RAG Use Cases + Advanced RAG
01.4Chapter 1 · Introduction to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

RAG Use Cases + Advanced RAG

LLMs ki power ko private data ke saath augment karne ki ability RAG ko lagbhag har us situation me applicable banati hai jahan ek enterprise ke andar LLM use hoga — kyunki zyadaatar enterprise applications ko apne private data tak access chahiye hota hai. Standalone tools ke roop me general chatbots employees ke liye useful hain — coding, marketing ya general world knowledge wale tasks me productivity badhane ke liye. Lekin kisi bhi application me jahan LLM ko internal data tak access chahiye, RAG best hai.

Virtual assistants aur AI chatbots

Virtual assistants aur chatbots customer interaction ki first line ke roop me serve kar sakte hain. Woh ya to customers se directly interact karne wala external tool ho sakte hain, ya customer service associates ko support karne wala internal tool. Ek simplified example: ek airline me customer support agents apne daily tasks me madad ke liye ek virtual assistant use kar sakte hain, jo phone par customers se baat karte waqt aane wale common questions ke jawab deta hai. Ek alag chatbot externally deploy kiya ja sakta hai, jo airline customers ko unke kisi bhi sawaal ke saath directly serve karta hai. Is use case me aap apni RAG application ko relevant internal knowledge bases ki taraf point karte hain — jaise previous customer support logs, airline FAQ ya website information, aur company policies ke aas-paas ke dusre internal documents. Aise virtual assistants deploy karne se customer service metrics par aksar positive impact dikhta hai — response times dramatically kam hote hain, support tickets ka overall volume kam hota hai, aur first-contact resolution rates badhte hain. Har interaction sabse current aur comprehensive data se informed hoti hai, jisse overall customer experience elevate hota hai.

Education me tutoring — ek khaas example

Education me bhi wahi pattern kaam karta hai. Universities aur schools ek chatbot deploy kar sakte hain jo student questions ke jawab dene me madad kare. Har student ke liye har waqt teacher ya tutor available hona lagbhag impossible hai. RAG se bana AI assistant har student ko kisi bhi subject ke liye, kabhi bhi aur kahin bhi, ek teacher de sakta hai — bas RAG system ko teacher ke authorized ya banaye hue course materials, jaise textbooks ya notes, se connect kar dein; phir assistant aise resources ke scope me student ke questions ke jawab de payega. Ek RAG-powered intelligent tutoring aur adaptive learning platform me pehle course materials ingestion server me feed kiye jate hain, jo unhe process karke vector DB me store karta hai. Phir agent student ke saath chatting ke through interact karta hai — tutor ke roop me ya examiner ke roop me. Tutor mode me student questions poochta hai aur agent jawab deta hai; har question ke liye agent apna LLM mobilize karta hai aur vector DB ko query karke answer generate karta hai. Examiner mode me woh proactively student ke liye questions generate karta hai aur unke responses ko grade karta hai. Woh improvement ki zaroorat wale areas ke basis par naye questions bhi generate kar sakta hai, taaki student ki chosen knowledge ki understanding reinforce ho.

Enterprise knowledge management aur internal search

Enterprise setting me employees ko aksar vast aur diverse data sources ke beech sahi information dhoondhne me challenge hota hai — khaas taur par jab data multiple systems me store hota hai: Google Drive, Notion, Salesforce, HubSpot, Jira, Confluence, aur aise hi kai files. RAG enterprise search ko modernize karta hai — retrieval ki strength (jo traditional enterprise search systems me common thi) ko LLM ke saath combine karke, jo generation aur information processing/reasoning capabilities add karta hai. Saare relevant enterprise data sources ko apni RAG application me ingest karke, jab employee ek query submit karta hai — policy details, historical meeting documents, ya technical specifications ke baare me — to system sabse relevant content extract karta hai, aur phir ek clear response generate karta hai. Ye process traditional, aksar time-consuming process ko replace karta hai — search ke top 10 results dekhna, har document ko padhna, aur apne dimaag me ek coherent aur accurate response banane ki koshish karna. Companies ko is approach se manifold benefits milte hain: employees woh time bachate hain jo numerous documents sift karne me lagta, aur critical information miss karne se bachte hain. Ye efficiency gain overall productivity boost karta hai aur teams ko administrative searches ke bajaye higher-value tasks par focus karne deta hai. Data sources ko continuously refreshed aur up to date rakhne se RAG-based knowledge management systems organization ke andar rapid changes ke saath pace rakhte hain.

Automated content creation aur document summarization

Enterprises me content creation bahut common hai — internal reports generate karna, marketing articles ya blog posts banana. Aise tasks me aksar meticulous research aur fact-checking chahiye hoti hai. RAG is creation process ko automate karke ek powerful solution deta hai. Jab content generate karne ka task diya jata hai, to RAG system multiple sources se latest, relevant data retrieve karta hai aur use well-structured drafts ya summaries produce karne ke liye use karta hai, jinhe zaroorat padne par ek human review kar sakta hai. Isse manual research ke liye chahiye hone wala time aur effort dramatically kam ho sakta hai, aur aksar zyada accurate content milta hai. Positive impact brand reputation tak bhi extend hota hai. Accurate aur promptly generated content ke saath, companies saare channels me ek consistent aur authoritative voice maintain kar sakti hain. Responsiveness aur reliability ka ye level legacy processes ke comparison me ek major competitive advantage ho sakta hai, jo zyada waqt lete hain aur kam accurate artifacts dete hain.

Personalized ads generate karna

Advertisements attractive aur effective hone chahiye. Conventionally, wahi ad saare target audiences ko deliver kiya jata hai, bina ye factor kiye ki user online kya kar raha hai ya kis baare me baat kar raha hai. RAG se hum zyada up-to-date aur personalized information wale ads generate kar sakte hain jo person to person differ karte hain aur potentially zyada effective hote hain. Ek RAG-powered system user context ke basis par on the fly compelling ads generate kar sakta hai — jaise user kis baare me chat kar raha tha, kya dekh raha tha, ya kya browse kar raha tha. Example ke liye, agar user running ke baare me chat kar raha hai, to running ya sports se related products pre-ingested vector DB se pull kiye jayenge, aur product information aur user ke baare me context (jaise unki previous purchases) dono ka use karke ek personalized ad generate kiya jayega. RAG-powered ad generation ka advantage clear hai: hum production recommendations ke liye RAG me powerful semantic search use kar sakte hain, aur sirf products dikhane ke bajaye un products ke liye ads create kar sakte hain jo user ke baare me hum jo jaante hain, usse match karte hain. Isse har ad individual users ke liye sabse relevant selling points emphasize karta hai. Example: ek shoe brand jo safety aur hygiene dono ke liye design kiya gaya hai — ek user jo haal me foot odor ke baare me chat kar raha tha aur ab soccer ke baare me baat kar raha hai, uske liye ad odor pain point ko address karke shuru ho sakta hai; dusre user jo safety ke baare me baat kar raha tha, uske liye ad reflective strips wali safety par focus kar sakta hai.

Question-answering systems

Question-answering systems user queries ke precise answers deliver karne ke liye design kiye jate hain — diverse datasets se information synthesize karke, RAG ka use karke. Chatbots ya virtual assistants ke unlike, jo multiturn conversations support karte hain, yahan form factor ek single question aur single answer ka hai. Ek common use case hai requests for proposals (RFPs) ya requests for information (RFIs) ka jawab dene me madad karna. Competitive sales landscape me customer inquiries aur proposal requests ka jawab dene me speed aur accuracy critical hoti hai. Jab sales team ko ek tailored proposal taiyaar karna hota hai, to RAG system internal databases se relevant historical data, product specifications, pricing details aur customer interactions pull karta hai, aur phir ek coherent, customized response construct karta hai. Positive impact clear hai: sales teams manual processes ke comparison me ek fraction time me high-quality proposals produce kar sakti hain, jisse responsiveness aur competitiveness badhti hai. Ye automation human error ka risk minimize karta hai aur ensure karta hai ki har proposal latest aur sabse accurate data se backed hai — pichhle proposal se copy-paste karne ke bajaye, jahan data up to date nahi bhi ho sakta — jisse win rates improve hote hain aur customer relationships mazboot hote hain.

Medical aur healthcare applications

Healthcare sector me timely aur accurate information life aur death ka matter ho sakta hai. Jab ek clinician ko treatment guidelines ya patient histories jaldi review karni hoti hain, to ek RAG application relevant case studies, research articles, aur patient ka medical record aur saare physician notes retrieve karke ek concise, evidence-based response generate kar sakti hai. Woh response har physician ki specialty ke hisaab se tailor bhi kiya ja sakta hai — example ke liye, summary alag hogi agar aap cardiovascular surgeon hain ya dermatology specialist — har ek ke liye relevant information alag hoti hai. Accurate aur contextualized medical summary dekar — historical medical records ko up-to-date medical information ke saath combine karke — hum physicians ko patients treat karne me zyada effective hone me madad kar sakte hain, allergy jaise critical information miss hone ki likelihood kam kar sakte hain, aur overall patients ko behtar treatment de sakte hain. Healthcare providers aur insurance companies ke liye benefits substantial hain: informed decisions lene ke liye chahiye hone wala time kam hota hai, patient outcomes improve hote hain, aur RAG systems clinicians ke cognitive load ko kam karne me madad karte hain — overwhelming raw data ke bajaye synthesized, aasani se digest hone wali information present karke. Aur patients ko zyada precise aur personalized care milti hai. Aise powerful applications ko production me deploy karna do non-negotiable principles par predicated hai: patient privacy protect karne ke liye Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) compliance ka rigorous adherence, aur ek robust "human-in-the-loop" (HITL) framework taaki ek qualified clinician AI ke output ko hamesha validate kare, usse pehle ki woh life-critical decision ko inform kare.

Legal aur compliance research

Healthcare aur financial services jaise kai regulated industries ko various laws aur regulations comply karna hota hai. Har legal requirement aur regulation ki full complexity samajhna, aur ye ki woh aapke business par kaise apply hoti hai, aksar complex hota hai aur legal research chahiye hoti hai jahan precision aur reliability paramount hain, kyunki errors significant financial ya reputational damage la sakti hain. Ek RAG-based system legal aur regulatory professionals ki madad kar sakta hai — relevant case law, statutes aur internal compliance documents jaldi retrieve karke. Ye approach traditional legal research methods se bahut improve karti hai, jo aksar legal texts aur databases aur internal data sources me manual searches par rely karte hain. Legal professionals ke liye benefits immense hain: research process ke ek significant portion ko automate karke, RAG legal opinions, compliance reports aur case preparations par faster turnaround times enable karta hai. Ye efficiency labor costs kam karti hai aur critical information overlook karne ke risk ko minimize karti hai.

Advanced RAG — aage kya hai

2020 me ek mashhoor research paper me pehli baar introduce hua RAG ek simple concept tha — text-only data tak limited, fine-tuning use karta tha in-context learning ke bajaye. Us foundational vision ne technology ke future development ka rasta banaya. Tab se RAG ek zyada advanced aur powerful form me progress kar chuka hai. Baaki book me advanced techniques cover hongi jaise agentic RAG, multimodal RAG aur knowledge graphs. Yahan unka ek quick overview hai.

Agentic RAG

Agentic RAG RAG ka ek evolution hai: relevant information retrieve karke response generate karne ki one-shot process ke bajaye, agentic RAG pipeline me autonomous AI agents incorporate karta hai. Ye agents aisi capabilities add karte hain:

  • Iterative aur multi-step retrieval: context sirf ek baar fetch karne ke bajaye, agents re-retrieve aur refine kar sakte hain agar initial data kaafi nahi hai.
  • Dynamic tool integration: agentic RAG multiple external tools (jaise web search ya API calls) leverage kar sakta hai varied sources of knowledge access karne ke liye, sirf pre-ingested knowledge par rely karne ke bajaye. Apne simplest form me, agentic RAG RAG me retrieval ko ek tool bana deta hai jise model ek ya zyada baar call kar sakta hai, jisse agent user query reformulate kar sakta hai ya multiturn conversations enable kar sakta hai, jahan previous exchanges ki information responses improve karne ke liye leverage ki ja sakti hai.
  • Advanced reasoning aur adaptability: agents complex queries decompose kar sakte hain, retrieval strategies plan kar sakte hain, information validate kar sakte hain, aur multi-part tasks handle karne ke liye specialized subagents ke beech coordinate bhi kar sakte hain.

Agentic RAG complex, multi-faceted queries handle karne ke liye zyada flexibility aur robustness deta hai — kai retrieval aur reasoning steps ko dynamically orchestrate karke.

Multimodal RAG

Shuru me RAG sirf textual information ke saath use hota tha. Tab se RAG ko dusri modalities tak expand kar diya gaya hai, jaise tables, diagrams aur charts. In dusri modalities ko incorporate karne ke usually do approaches hain. Pehla approach hai saari information modalities ko text me convert karna (jaise images ko unke captions me), aur phir well-understood RAG pipeline ko sirf text domain me chalana. Dusra hai multimodal embedding models aur language models, jaise vision-language models (VLMs) ya multimodal large language models (MLLMs), leverage karna. Is approach me non-textual domains ki information apni original modality me rehti hai. Ye information phir query time par VLM ko provide ki jati hai aur textual data ke saath response generate karne ke liye use ki jati hai. Ek aur end-to-end approach jo haal me rise par hai, woh hai poora page embed karna aur pages ko response generate karne ke liye MLLM me bhejna.

RAG with knowledge graphs

Ab tak discuss kiye gaye RAG examples digitized text ko as-is use karte hain. Ye conventional approach complex datasets me "dots connect karne" me struggle kar sakta hai. Is limitation ko address karne ke liye ek advanced strategy hai knowledge graphs (KGs) leverage karna. Flat text embeddings par rely karne ke bajaye, KGs integrate karne me pehle unstructured documents ko process karke key entities aur unke relationships extract kiye jate hain. Ye connections phir ek knowledge graph construct karne ke liye use hote hain. Ye structured representation system ko multi-hop reasoning support karne deti hai (alag-alag pieces of information connect karna, aksar multiple documents me, aise conclusions tak pahunchne ke liye jo ek single source se obvious nahi hain) aur complex queries ka jawab dete waqt deeper context awareness provide karti hai. Ek mashhoor approach jise Microsoft ne popularize kiya hai, woh hai GraphRAG — KGs ko manually build karne ki complexity address karne ke liye propose kiya gaya. GraphRAG pehle unstructured documents ko process karke entities aur relationships extract karta hai, aur ek knowledge graph construct karta hai jo data ke andar inherent connections capture karta hai.

Yaad rakho: RAG ka har use case ek hi pattern hai — private data + LLM. Chatbot ho, internal search ho, RFP jawab ho ya medical summary — farq sirf data aur stakes ka hai. Aur advanced RAG (agentic, multimodal, knowledge graphs) wahi pattern ko complex, multi-step aur multi-format queries tak le jata hai.
SOURCESource: Hands-On RAG for Production, O'Reilly, Chapter 1 — Introduction to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
← Previous01.3 · Key Benefits of RAG→ Next02 · The Base RAG Stack — do flows
02Chapter 2 · The Base RAG Stack

The Base RAG Stack — do flows

Chapter 1 me humne RAG ka core idea introduce kiya — large language models ko sirf training par rely karne ke bajaye external knowledge access karne dena. Is chapter me hum un technical components me deeper dive karte hain jo ek RAG system ko practice me function karne dete hain. Ye components ek pipeline banate hain — jise RAG stack kehte hain — jo raw documents taiyaar karne se lekar high-quality, context-grounded responses generate karne tak jaati hai.

Do flows — ingestion aur query

Basic RAG stack me do major flows hote hain. Ingestion flow usually ek baar chalaya jata hai jab naya data available hota hai ya existing data update karna hota hai. Query flow har baar trigger hota hai jab user RAG system ko query bhejta hai, aur ingestion flow me taiyaar kiye gaye data ka use karke user queries ka jawab deta hai. In flows ka har step — parsing, chunking, embedding, indexing, vector search, reranking aur LLM-based generation — ek distinct role play karta hai aur apne trade-offs laata hai. In pieces ko samajhna errors diagnose karne, quality improve karne aur scalable RAG architectures design karne ke liye essential hai jo production environments me predictably behave karein.

Ingestion flow — chaar steps

Ingestion flow me source documents pre-process kiye jate hain (parse aur chunk kiye jate hain), aur is pre-processing ka product aise store kiya jata hai jo baad me efficient searching aur retrieval enable kare, taaki LLM kisi task ko fulfill kar sake ya user query ka jawab de sake. Ingestion flow typically chaar steps se banta hai: parsing, chunking, embedding aur indexing. Production systems me ye steps typically asynchronously orchestrate kiye jate hain, retries ke saath.

Ingestion ke data sources — structured vs unstructured

Ingestion ke liye data various sources se aa sakta hai, jaise databases, files (local ya cloud), APIs, ya web scraping. Databases aur APIs se data generally ingest karna aasan hota hai kyunki woh structured hota hai — schema (fields aur data types define karta hai) pehle se pata hota hai. Example ke liye, agar aap LLM aur users ke beech conversations ingest kar rahe hain, to pehle se pata hai ki har message me ek role field hai (message LLM se hai ya user se), ek timestamp hai, aur message text bhi hai, aur ek conversation aise compound message objects ki list hai. Aise data ki preprocessing usually easy aur minimal hoti hai — jaise nested structure ko flatten karna aur un fields ko discard karna jo aapke RAG tasks ke liye useful nahi hain. Conversations wale example me hum conversations ko chaar columns ki 2D table me flatten kar sakte hain: message text, role (message kisne bheja — user ya LLM), timestamp, aur conversation ID (jo same conversation se belong karne wale messages ko correspond karne ke liye use hota hai). Sirf message text hi aage semantic search ke liye embed kiya jayega.

Iske contrast me, files ki preprocessing (pure text files jaise .txt ko chhod kar) zyada complex ho sakti hai, kyunki woh various formats me aa sakti hain (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, HTML, aadi), jinme RAG ko operate karne ke liye chahiye hone wali information se zyada information hoti hai. Example ke liye, Microsoft Word documents me formatting aur styling information usually RAG ke liye meaningful nahi hoti, aur isliye use identify karke discard karna padta hai. Files ingest karne me ek aur challenge ye hai ki aapko chahiye hone wala textual ya tabular data scanned images include kar sakta hai, jinhe text extract karne ke liye optical character recognition (OCR) jaisi techniques chahiye hoti hain. Alag-alag modalities aur purposes ki information ko separate karke sirf woh extract karne ke process ko parsing kehte hain.

Parsing se chunking tak — kyun todna padta hai

Parsing se discrete text segments milte hain jo LLM ko accurate responses generate karne ke liye necessary context provide karte hain. Lekin ye segments aksar bahut lambe hote hain, jinhe LLM ek baar me process nahi kar sakta — context window size, cost aur LLMs ki effectiveness jaise reasons se. Zyadaatar questions ko lengthy raw segments ke sirf ek chhote fraction par attend karne ki zaroorat hoti hai. Ek lengthy context sirf wasteful nahi hai, balki backfire bhi kar sakta hai — jaise retrieval effectiveness kam karke. Isliye hume unhe chhote pieces me todna padta hai jinhe chunks kehte hain. Chunks me todne ke process ko chunking kehte hain.

Chunking se embedding tak — searchable banana

Is point tak aapka data apne original form me rehta hai (ek text abhi bhi characters ki linear sequence hai), jo searching aur retrieval ko ineffective bana sakta hai. Example ke liye, agar aapki query text "United States" hai, to aap use character space me directly "USA" se match nahi kar payenge. Ya agar aapki query text "Silicon Valley" hai, to aap Chinese documents jinme uska Chinese naam hai, unhe string comparison se directly nahi dhoondh payenge. Searchability improve karne ka ek tareeka hai text ko numbers ke vector me convert karna jo uske semantic meaning ko capture kare. Is process aur uske output ko embedding (ya zyada precisely, dense embedding ya vector embedding) kehte hain. Embedding ke alawa, searchability improve karne ke dusre tareeke bhi hain bina data representation ya format transform kiye — jaise inverted indices ya keyword-based indexing. Ye methods zyada traditional hain aur aksar search engines me use hote hain, lekin woh text ke semantic meaning ko embeddings jitna effectively capture nahi kar sakte. Lekin woh kuch scenarios me embeddings ko complement kar sakte hain — jaise kisi particular business ke naam wale contracts dhoondhna jiska naam pehle kabhi dekha hi nahi gaya, ya user queries me typos tolerate karna, jahan keyword-based indexing similar terms match karne me madad kar sakti hai. Embedding ke saath, information ko transform aur organize karne ke saare methods — taaki baad me fast aur easy retrieval ho — indexing ke umbrella ke neeche aate hain, jo bade datasets me search karte waqt fast lookups aur resources ka efficient use allow karta hai. Representation of information searchability improve karne ka sirf pehla step hai. Dense embeddings ke liye agla step hai in embeddings ko aise store karna jo efficient retrieval allow kare — aur yahin vector databases aati hain.

Query flow — query rewriting se shuru

Ingestion flow ke baad, RAG stack ingested data ka use karke user ki query ka jawab dene ke liye taiyaar hai. Query ek question, command, instructions ki sequence, ya koi bhi task ho sakta hai jo aap RAG stack se karwana chahte hain. Example: "Write a poem based on my travels in 2025." RAG ki power isme hai ki woh LLMs ko aisi queries ka jawab dene deta hai jinhe training data me unseen knowledge chahiye hota hai. Ek off-the-shelf LLM ko nahi pata hoga ki aap kaun hain, na ki aap 2025 me kahan the. Lekin agar aapne apni 2025 diary ya blog posts RAG stack me ingest kar liye hain, to woh un documents se aapke 2025 travels ke baare me information retrieve karke LLM ko de sakta hai, taaki woh un par based ek poem generate kare.

Query flow ka pehla step hai query rewriting — user query ko aise format me transform karne ka process jo LLM ki performance improve kare. Example ke liye, query "Write a poem based on my travels in 2025" ke do parts hain: "Write a poem" aur "based on my travels in 2025." Pehla part ek command hai, dusra part woh context hai jo retrieve karke LLM ko fulfill karne ke liye bhejna hai. Agar "write a poem" ko retrieval query me include kar diya jaye, to woh irrelevant results la sakta hai — jaise travel aur 2025 ke baare me nahi, balki poems retrieve karna — aur travel aur 2025 ke baare me non-poem info chhoot sakti hai. Phir LLM aapko dusri poems par based poem de sakta hai, lekin travel ya 2025 ke baare me nahi. Isliye hume query ko rewrite karna padta hai taaki woh context part par focus kare, jo hai "my travels in 2025." Information retrieval ke liye use hone wali query ko retrieval query kehte hain, taaki use original user query se distinguish kiya ja sake.

Retrieval — semantic search aur keyword search

Agla step hai retrieval query ke basis par relevant information retrieve karna. Usually do search categories hoti hain: semantic search (dense retrieval bhi kehte hain) aur keyword search (sparse retrieval bhi kehte hain). Semantic search me retrieval query ko embedding vector me convert kiya jata hai, jo phir vector database me similar vectors search karne ke liye use hota hai. Do vectors ke beech similarity ko efficiently measure kiya ja sakta hai ek mathematical operation se jise dot product kehte hain (inner product ya scalar product bhi kehte hain). Aaj ke embedding models lagbhag saare normalized ya unit embedding vectors produce karte hain, jin ki magnitude 1 hoti hai. Jab dot product operation me do vectors unit vectors hote hain, to dot product cosine similarity ke barabar hota hai, jo measure karta hai ki do vectors ki directions kitni aligned hain. Keyword search techniques ka ek group hai, jaise term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) aur BM25 (BM ka matlab best matching), jo semantic search se bahut pehle develop hue the. Semantic search ke unlike, jise strings ko vectors me convert karna padta hai aur vector space par operate karna padta hai, keyword search directly strings match karta hai, aur is tarah lexicon space me operate karta hai. Modern embedding models words ya phrases ko represent karne wale vectors bhi generate kar sakte hain matching purposes ke liye. Aise vectors ko dense embedding vectors se distinguish karne ke liye hum unhe sparse vectors kehte hain. Dono semantic aur keyword searches ki strengths aur weaknesses hain. Dono ke best ko combine karne ke liye aap dono ka combination use kar sakte hain, jise hybrid search kehte hain. Base stack me (jo is chapter ka subject hai) hum pure semantic search par focus karte hain, jabki hybrid search (rare tokens, typos aur exact-match constraints par behtar robustness ke liye) Chapter 3 me discuss hoga.

Reranking — top-k hi kaafi nahi hota

Cost aur effectiveness ke reasons se, hum sabse relevant aur informative chunks pick karke LLM ko feed karna chahte hain. Ye aasan lagta hai, hai na? Bas chunks ko retrieval query ke saath unke similarity scores ke basis par rank karo aur top wale pick kar lo. Durbhagya se, ye itna simple nahi hai. Kai reasons hain ki embedding models se ranking LLM ke liye optimal nahi bhi ho sakti, aur isliye hum aksar reranking ka ek additional step apply karte hain. Pehle, retrieval models multiple chunks return kar sakte hain jo redundant information convey karte hain. In sab ko LLM ko bhejna token budget aur computation dono waste karta hai. Ye problem LLMs ke emergence se bahut pehle se observe ki gayi hai. Maximum marginal relevance (MMR) reranker, jo selected chunks me redundancy kam karne ke liye relevance ko diversity ke saath balance karta hai, 1998 me develop hua tha. Dusre, semantic search ke liye, embedding-based retrieval me use hone wale dot product similarity scores LLM ke underlying attention mechanism ko fully exploit nahi karte. Embedding models har text ko independently represent karte hain, aur unki similarity post hoc vector operations se measure ki jati hai. Iske contrast me, transformer-based rerankers query aur candidate chunk ko jointly evaluate karte hain, jisse cross-attention do texts ke beech nuanced relationships, context alignment aur semantic relevance ko behtar capture kar sakta hai. Retrieval khatm hone ke baad, hum aakhirkaar chunks ko generative LLM ko bhejne ke liye taiyaar hain, jo original user query ko retrieved chunks ke context me inspect karke response generate karega.

Yaad rakho: Ingestion flow ek baar chalta hai (parse → chunk → embed → index) aur query flow har query par chalta hai (rewrite → retrieve → rerank → generate). Retrieval query original user query se alag hoti hai — woh sirf woh hissa hoti hai jo data dhoondhne ke liye chahiye.
SOURCESource: Hands-On RAG for Production, O'Reilly, Chapter 2 — The Base RAG Stack
← Previous01.4 · RAG Use Cases + Advanced RAG→ Next02.1 · Document Parsing
02.1Chapter 2 · The Base RAG Stack

Document Parsing

Aksar woh text data jo aap RAG me use karna chahte hain, simple text format me nahi hota, balki PDF, PPTX, DOCX, HTML aur Markdown jaise formats me hota hai. In formats me woh text jo aapke RAG queries ka jawab dene ke liye knowledge contain karta hai, aksar typesetting/styling information, jaise fonts, ke saath mix hota hai, jo aapke RAG queries ka jawab dene ke liye useful nahi bhi ho sakta. Jo step us text ko separate karta hai jo RAG me use karne wala knowledge contain karta hai, baaki sab se — use document parsing kehte hain. Ise parsing isliye kehte hain kyunki aise formats designated syntaxes ya structures follow karte hain, jaise ek computer program, aur hume syntactically determine karna padta hai ki text ke kaunse segments woh knowledge contain karte hain jo hum RAG me use karna chahte hain. Is stage par sahi tareeke se parse karna critical hai, kyunki ingestion me koi bhi error ya inconsistency RAG system ke knowledge base ki integrity aur reliability ko compromise kar degi, aur quality responses dene ki uski ability ko bhi.

PDF — sabse challenging format

PDF files RAG me ingest kiye jane wale sabse common types ke documents me se ek hain, aur sabse challenging bhi. PDF fundamentally ek document ki visual appearance render karne ke liye design kiya gaya tha, uski logical structure ke liye nahi. Is reason se zyadaatar PDF files me koi schema ya hierarchical content nahi hota — sirf tagged PDF files exception hain, jo accessibility reasons ke liye design ki gayi hain aur jinme structure hota hai. Ek word individual characters ke collection ke roop me store hota hai, jin ke 2D coordinates hote hain, aur isiliye text extraction itna challenging hai. Words, sentences ya paragraphs extract karne ke liye complex algorithms chahiye hote hain jo characters ke coordinates ke beech relationships analyze karte hain. Example ke liye, ye batane ke liye ki ek page me do columns hain ya nahi, aapko page ke saare characters ki clustering aur alignment analyze karni padti hai. Warna aap do columns ke beech lines mix kar sakte hain, jisse meaningless sentences ban jayengi.

PDF parsing ke liye libraries

Khushkismati se, madad ke liye kai libraries hain. Popular libraries me pypdf (jis ki history me PyPDF2, PyPDF3 aur PyPDF4 shamil hain), PyMuPDF aur pdfminer.six (PDFMiner ka community edition) aate hain. PDF ke inventor ki commercial product PDF Extract API bhi hai jo ek PDF file ko JSON string me parse karti hai, aur kuch startups bhi PDF extractors offer karte hain. Aksar ek PDF file scanned documents se originate karti hai, jahan har page ek picture hota hai. Aise pages se textual ya tabular info nikaalne ke liye OCR utilize karna padta hai. Tesseract OCR ke liye sabse famous open source libraries me se ek hai, aur bade cloud providers bhi OCR APIs offer karte hain. Iske alawa kai startups bhi OCR par focused hain. OCR accuracy heavily depend karti hai image quality (resolution aur clarity), fonts ki complexity aur style, aur layout par.

DOCX aur HTML — XML family, aasan lekin dhyaan se

PDF ke comparison me DOCX ya HTML formats ke saath kaam karna relatively aasan hai, kyunki woh XML formats ki family se belong karte hain, jahan information aur unke attributes (jaise font size, color, aadi) interleaved hote hain aur structured tareeke se store hote hain. Example ke liye, HTML me text "The capital of France is Paris." ko bold tag ke saath represent kiya jata hai, jahan tag indicate karta hai ki "Paris" bold me display hona chahiye. Lekin query "What is the capital of France?" ka jawab dete waqt woh bold tag shayad chahiye nahi hota. Isliye parsing ke dauraan hum tag discard karke sirf text return karna chahte hain. DOCX aur HTML files se text parse aur extract karne ke liye kai libraries available hain, jaise DOCX files ke liye python-docx aur HTML files ke liye Beautiful Soup. PDF files ki tarah, DOCX ya HTML bhi container formats hain jinme tables ya images jaisa multimodal data include ho sakta hai.

Tags hamesha discard karne layak nahi hote — metadata

Ye hamesha sach nahi hota ki tags aur attributes discard karne chahiye. Kuch tags ya attributes pipeline me aage useful clues provide kar sakte hain. Maan lo process karne wala text ek chat log hai, jisme har message ek div hai jis ki class batati hai ki woh user ka hai ya AI ka, aur id batati hai ki kaunsa message hai. Agar hum tags aur attributes discard kar dein, to hum ye context kho dete hain ki kisne kya kaha aur kab. Baad me, agar query hai "AI ke according, France ke President kahan rehte hain?", to hum jawab nahi de payenge. Ek behtar solution hai class ko metadata ke roop me record karna. Metadata text segment ke baare me additional information hai jo context ya dusri useful information provide karne ke liye use ki ja sakti hai. Example me "What is the capital of France?" ke saath metadata hoga ki woh user ne kaha, aur "The capital of France is Paris." ke saath metadata hoga ki woh AI ne kaha. Query rewriting ke dauraan aap ab query ko split kar sakte hain — ek main query ("France ke President kahan rehte hain") jo semantic search ke liye use hogi, aur ek metadata filter jo "who" ko "AI" value par constrain karta hai; is tarah user ke messages, chahe unhone French capital ke baare me kuch kaha ho, retrieval se exclude ho jayenge. Metadata filtering ek database operation hai jo SQL me where clause jaisi hoti hai — iska semantic search se koi lena-dena nahi hai.

Vision-language models se parsing

Aaj ke LLMs non-textual data bhi process kar sakte hain. Textual data hi process karne wale LLM se distinguish karne ke liye hum kabhi-kabhi vision-language models (VLMs) term use karte hain — aisa model jo visual information (still images ya videos) aur texts dono process kar sakta hai. Ek VLM ko various file formats ko directly parse karne ke liye leverage kiya ja sakta hai. Ye approach khaas taur par complex layouts wale documents ke liye useful hai, jaise slides, forms ya infographics. Lekin is option ko bahut caution ke saath use karein. VLMs text extract karne me hamesha accurate nahi bhi ho sakte. Apni generative nature ki wajah se woh hallucination ke prone hote hain, aur aaj ke samay me aksar unhe diye gaye documents me images reproduce nahi kar sakte. Bade, enterprise-scale datasets ke liye VLM use karke parsing karna kaafi mehenga aur slow bhi ho sakta hai. Isliye ye approach mushkil, high-value document types ke liye reserve karni chahiye, ya fallback ke roop me jab classical parsers fail ho jayein. Recommendation hai ek "cheapest successful parser-first" strategy — pehle PDF libraries, HTML parsers, OCR, aur uske baad hi VLM call karein.

Code examples — kya karte hain (prose me)

Book me teen coding examples ke through parsing dikhaya gaya hai. Pehla, PyMuPDF se PDF files parse karna: library characters ko unki proximity ke basis par group karti hai. Poore page ka text ek string ke roop me extract karne se table ka text regular unstructured text ke saath mix ho jata hai — jo ideal nahi hai. Text ko block ke hisaab se extract karne se boundaries clear hoti hain, lekin phir bhi ye nahi bataya ja sakta ki kaunsa block table ka hai aur kaunsa regular text ka. Isliye pehle tables extract kiye jate hain — table find karke use 2D Python list ke roop me extract kiya jata hai (rows sublists hote hain) — aur phir table contents ko saare text se subtract karke sirf unstructured text hasil kiya jata hai. Table ke bounding box ke andar ka text nikaal kar, page text ko lines me split karke aur table content wali lines ko filter out karke clean paragraph text milta hai. PDF se images extract karna thoda complicated hai, kyunki images "external" information mani jati hain: image list function asal me images ki binary representations nahi deta, balki images ki "pointer" info deta hai; extract function hi image data asal me image ke reference number (xref) ka use karke leta hai. Dusra, python-docx se DOCX files parse karna: DOCX ek structured format hai jo document ke elements ka metadata retain karta hai, aur asal me XML files aur media files ka ek ZIP archive hota hai. Library se paragraphs ka text aur tables extract kiye jate hain, aur ZIP archive ke andar image files ko unke common extensions (.jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif) se search karke images extract ki jati hain. Teesra, ek LLM se PDF parse karna: PDF file upload karke plain English instructions di jati hain — pehle tables ya images ke texts ko exclude karke sirf text content extract karo, phir tables extract karke Markdown tables ke roop me return karo. LLM ko di gayi message ke do parts hote hain: parse karne wali file, aur instructions.

Yaad rakho: Parsing me accuracy sabse pehle aati hai — ingestion ki galti aage kabhi theek nahi hoti. Pehle cheapest parser try karo, metadata ko mat phenko (woh filter ka kaam karta hai), aur VLM ko sirf mushkil documents ya fallback ke liye rakho.
parse-docx.ipynb — Parsing DOCX Documents — GitHub: ofermend/hands-on-rag, chapter2/parse-docx.ipynb (https://github.com/ofermend/hands-on-rag/blob/main/chapter2/parse-docx.ipynb)
import os
from docx import Document
from IPython.display import display, Image

document = Document('sample_data/sample_data.docx')

# extract text 
for para in document.paragraphs:
  if len(para.text.strip()) > 0:  # Only print non-empty paragraphs
    print(para.text, end="\n---\n") 

# extract tables
for table in document.tables:
  print("\n--- Table ---")
  for row in table.rows:
    row_text = [cell.text for cell in row.cells]
    print(row_text)

import zipfile

zipf = zipfile.ZipFile('sample_data/sample_data.docx')
filelist = zipf.namelist()
# print (filelist)

for fname in filelist:
  _, ext = os.path.splitext(fname)
  if ext in ['.jpg', '.jpeg', '.png', '.gif']:
    # read image and display in Jupyter
    with zipf.open(fname) as img_file:
        img_data = img_file.read()
        display(Image(data=img_data))

# Visualize the extracted image
import base64
from PIL import Image
from io import BytesIO

image_base64 = completion.choices[0].message.content
image_data = base64.b64decode(image_base64)
try:
    image = Image.open(BytesIO(image_data))
    image.show()
except Exception:
    print("LLM-generated base64 is not a valid image.")
    print("LLMs cannot faithfully reproduce binary data — the base64 string is hallucinated.")
    print(f"Decoded size: {len(image_data)} bytes (real image is much larger)")
    print("\nUse PyMuPDF (next cell) to extract images from PDFs reliably.")

# Extract image using PyMuPDF, encode to base64, then visualize
import fitz  # PyMuPDF
import base64
from IPython.display import Image, display
import io

# Open the PDF file
pdf_path = "sample_data/sample_data.pdf"
pdf_document = fitz.open(pdf_path)

# Extract the first image found
for page_num in range(len(pdf_document)):
    page = pdf_document[page_num]
    image_list = page.get_images(full=True)
    
    if image_list:
        # Get the first image
        img = image_list[0]
        xref = img[0]
        pix = fitz.Pixmap(pdf_document, xref)
        
        # Convert to PNG bytes
        if pix.n - pix.alpha < 4:  # GRAY or RGB
            img_data = pix.tobytes("png")
        else:  # CMYK
            pix = fitz.Pixmap(fitz.csRGB, pix)
            img_data = pix.tobytes("png")
        
        # Encode to base64
        base64_string = base64.b64encode(img_data).decode('utf-8')
        print(f"Base64 string length: {len(base64_string)}")
        print(f"First 100 characters of base64: {base64_string[:100]}...")
        
        # Now decode the base64 string back and display
        decoded_img_data = base64.b64decode(base64_string)
        
        # Display the image from base64
        display(Image(data=decoded_img_data))
        print("Image successfully extracted, encoded to base64, and displayed!")
        
        pix = None  # Clean up
        break

pdf_document.close()

import json
import pymupdf
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Image, display
import io

# Extract all text on one page
with pymupdf.open("sample_data/sample_data.pdf") as doc:
  for page in doc:
    text: str = page.get_text()
#    print(text, end="---")

# Extract text in blocks
with pymupdf.open("sample_data/sample_data.pdf") as doc:
  for page in doc:
    text: str = page.get_text("blocks")
    for block in text:
      print(block[4], end="---\n")

# Extract table contents
with pymupdf.open("sample_data/sample_data.pdf") as doc:
  for page in doc: 
    tables = page.find_tables() # locate and extract any tables on page
    for i, table in enumerate(tables):
      print (f"Table {i+1}")
      print(table.extract(), end="\n\n")

# Extract non-table text
def extract_unstructured_text(pdf_path):
  """
  Extract unstructured text from PDF, excluding table content.
  Returns clean paragraph text without tabular data.
  """
  unstructured_text = []
  
  with pymupdf.open(pdf_path) as doc:
    for page in doc:
      # Get all text from the page
      page_text = page.get_text()
      
      # Find tables on the page to exclude their content
      tables = page.find_tables()
      
      # Get table text blocks to filter out
      table_text_blocks = []
      if tables.tables:
        for table in tables:
          # Get table bounding box
          bbox = table.bbox
          # Extract text within table bounds
          table_text = page.get_text(clip=bbox)
          table_text_blocks.append(table_text.strip())
      
      # Split page text into lines and filter out table content
      lines = page_text.split('\n')
      filtered_lines = []
      
      for line in lines:
        line = line.strip()
        if line:  # Skip empty lines
          # Check if this line is part of any table
          is_table_content = False
          for table_text in table_text_blocks:
            if line in table_text:
              is_table_content = True
              break
          
          # Only include non-table content
          if not is_table_content:
            filtered_lines.append(line)
      
      # Join filtered lines back into paragraphs
      page_unstructured = '\n'.join(filtered_lines)
      if page_unstructured.strip():
        unstructured_text.append(page_unstructured)
  
  return '\n\n'.join(unstructured_text)

# Test the function
unstructured_content = extract_unstructured_text("sample_data/sample_data.pdf")
print("Unstructured text extracted:")
print(unstructured_content)

# Extract images 
with pymupdf.open("sample_data/sample_data.pdf") as doc:
  for page in doc:
    # Get images from the page
    image_list = page.get_images()
    for image_index, img in enumerate(image_list):
      # Extract image data
      xref = img[0]
      base_image = doc.extract_image(xref)
      image_bytes = base_image["image"]
      # Display the image directly in Jupyter Notebook
      display(Image(data=image_bytes))

      # save image 
      image_format = base_image["ext"]
      with open(f"extracted_image_{page.number}_{image_index}.{image_format}", "wb") as img_file:
          img_file.write(image_bytes)
