05Chapter 5 · The RAG Platform

The RAG Platform — DIY vs Platform

Chapters 2 aur 3 me aapne do-it-yourself RAG seekha — embedding models aur vector databases jaise basic components se lekar hybrid search, reranking aur hallucination detection jaise advanced components tak. Chapter 4 me dekha ki DIY RAG application ko PoC se fully production-ready deployment tak le jaana aksar dikhne se zyada complex kyun hota hai. Ab ek aur raasta dekhte hain: RAG platform (jise RAG-as-a-service ya turnkey RAG bhi kehte hain) — ek technology platform jo RAG components ke zyadaatar ya saare hisse ko ek developer API ke peeche implement kar deta hai. Isse RAG banane ki complexity abstract ho jati hai, aur developers RAG application par focus kar sakte hain — responses kis data par grounded honi chahiye, aur application business ya application flow me kaise integrate hoti hai.

DIY RAG — granular control, poori zimmedari

DIY RAG stack banate waqt aapke paas RAG pipeline ke har component par granular control hota hai: vector databases select aur configure karna (jaise Pinecone, Weaviate, Zilliz, Qdrant), koi bhi embedding model host aur serve karna (jaise Cohere ka Embed v4 ya Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B), chunking strategies define aur implement karna, aur LLM generation process customize karna. Power aapke haath me hai — aur underlying infrastructure ko provision, integrate, scale aur maintain karne ki zimmedari bhi aapki hi hai.

RAG platform — managed, end-to-end solution

Iske contrast me RAG platform ek managed, end-to-end solution deta hai, infrastructure complexities ko abstract karke. Developers APIs ke through service se interact karte hain — data sources se data ingest karna, retrieval pipeline select aur configure karna, embedding ya generative models select karna, aur minimal setup ke saath RAG application deploy karna. Yahi infrastructure overhead se freedom RAG platforms ko edge deti hai: DIY approach me aap considerable effort non-core tasks par kharch karte hain — server provisioning, vector DB optimization, high availability aur low latency ensure karna, har component ke liye security updates manage karna. RAG platform providers ye operational overheads le lete hain, taaki aap sirf application logic banane aur end users ko value dene par focus kar sakein. Isse faster development cycles, kam DevOps workload aur potentially kam upfront infrastructure costs milti hain, kyunki services aksar pay-as-you-go ya subscription basis par milti hain. RAG platform aksar low latency, high accuracy aur cost effectiveness ke liye built-in optimizations ke saath aata hai, provider ki large-scale RAG systems manage karne ki expertise ka fayda uthate hue. Providers data source connectors, advanced monitoring aur observability, aur security aur privacy compliance out of the box bhi de sakte hain — jinhe DIY setup me replicate karne ke liye significant engineering effort chahiye hota. Ek RAG platform central control plane deta hai jo security, accuracy, cost aur performance par governance enable karta hai. Lekin is ease of use ke saath platform lock-in aur providers switch karne par potential migration costs ka risk bhi aata hai.

Middle ground — cloud providers ke "platforms of services"

DIY aur platform ke beech major cloud providers ek middle ground dete hain — "platforms of services" jaise Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, Google Cloud Vertex AI Search aur Azure AI Search. Ye powerful toolkits hain jo DIY ko simplify karte hain, lekin phir bhi developer ko multiple components select, configure aur orchestrate karne hote hain — jaise alag vector database wire karna ya retrieval aur generation API calls ko manually chain karna. Iske contrast me true end-to-end RAG platforms (jaise Vectara ya Nuclia) saare components (document extraction, chunking, embedding, vector storage, retrieval, generation aur hallucination detection) ko ek single, unified API me bundle kar dete hain, complexity ko developer se chhupa kar. Ab aapke paas components ki samajh hai (Chapters 2 aur 3 se), to aap apni organization ki needs ke hisaab se pros aur cons weigh karke informed decision le sakte hain — khud ka RAG system banayein ya RAG platform use karein.

Yaad rakho: DIY ka matlab hai maximum flexibility aur maximum zimmedari; platform ka matlab hai speed aur simplicity, lock-in ke risk ke saath. Faisla is par depend karta hai ki aapki team ko kya chahiye — control ya velocity — aur dono me se kis ki keemat aap chukane ko ready hain.
SOURCESource: Hands-On RAG for Production, O'Reilly, Chapter 5 — The RAG Platform
← Previous04.3 · Reference Production Architecture + PoC to Production→ Next05.1 · Core RAG Capabilities + Governance
05.1Chapter 5 · The RAG Platform

Core RAG Capabilities + Governance

DIY vs platform ka faisla lene se pehle har core capability ko alag-alag samajhna zaroori hai — kyunki har component par trade-off alag hota hai. Response ki quality ingestion aur query/retrieval pipeline dono ki capabilities par depend karti hai.

Embedding models — default, BYO aur dimensions

Bahut se RAG platforms ek default embedding model dete hain. Agar non-English languages support karni hain to embedding model ki dusri languages me support aur performance samajhna important hai. Kuch providers bring-your-own (BYO) embedding model support karte hain — isse comfort aur future risk mitigation milti hai: agar built-in embedding model future use case ke liye fit na ho to use naye model se replace kar sakte hain. Lekin yaad rakho — aapne saare data ke embedding vectors pehle hi generate kar liye hain, aur naya embedding model switch karne ka matlab hai poora dataset dobara encode karna, jo additional time aur cost add karta hai. Embedding models alag sizes (vector dimensions) me aate hain. Bade vector dimensions potentially zyada nuanced semantic detail capture kar sakte hain, jisse overall retrieval accuracy badh sakti hai — lekin hamesha itna impactful nahi hota, khaas taur par jab retrieval ke dusre step me strong reranking models hon. Computationally, higher-dimensionality vectors process karne me zyada expensive hote hain: indexing ke liye zyada computational power aur time chahiye (DIY setup me zyada powerful CPUs ya GPUs), aur querying bhi resource-intensive ho jati hai kyunki high-dimensional vectors ke beech similarity scores (jaise cosine similarity) calculate karne me zyada operations lagte hain — isse latency badh sakti hai ya performance banaye rakhne ke liye zyada compute instances chahiye hote hain. RAG platform me memory ya computational demands badhne ka bojh vendor par padta hai, aur woh typically pricing me reflect hota hai. Agar BYO embedding model requirement hai to vendor se poocho ki ye supported option hai ya nahi, aur samjho ki isse kya extra costs jud sakti hain.

Vector databases — control vs managed service

Apna RAG stack banate waqt aap open source vector database (jaise Milvus, Qdrant ya Weaviate) ya proprietary (jaise Pinecone) select kar sakte hain, ya Snowflake ya MongoDB jaise existing database ki vector feature use kar sakte hain. Jo bhi use karo, aapko indexing strategies, sharding aur hardware/cloud infrastructure selection par fine-grained control milta hai — apne specific data, query patterns aur performance requirements ke liye optimize karne ki flexibility, aur failure isolation behtar manage karne ki. Lekin is control ke saath setup, ongoing maintenance, scaling, security patching aur vector database management me in-house expertise ki zimmedari aati hai — significant operational overhead aur hidden costs, software open source hone ke baad bhi. Bade vector dimensions yahan bhi matter karte hain: zyada storage requirements, added costs aur higher latency. RAG platform vector database ko managed service ke hisse ke roop me bundle kar deta hai — setup, configuration, scaling, maintenance aur optimization ki complexities provider par chhod deta hai. Bade vectors ka impact platform ki cost par bhi padta hai, aur woh pricing me reflect ho sakta hai. Agar deep customization chahiye aur complex database infrastructure manage karne ki engineering talent hai to DIY achha option ho sakta hai; agar speed to market, ease of use aur operational burdens offload karna important hai, aur provider ki chosen vector database capabilities se comfortable hain, to RAG platform zyada efficient raasta ho sakta hai.

Advanced retrieval, prompt engineering aur multiple LLMs

  • Advanced retrieval: Robust aur accurate retrieval pipeline accurate results ke liye probably sabse impactful component hai. DIY stack me vector search se shuru karna common hai, phir hybrid search aur ek ya zyada reranking options se improve karna. Vector search vector database aur embedding model milne ke baad relatively easy hai, lekin hybrid search aur rerankers implement karna zyada mushkil kaam ho sakta hai — additional expertise, time aur effort mangta hai. Lekin yahi woh jagah hai jahan retrieval relevance aur system reliability me sabse bade gains milte hain. Retrieval pipeline ek critical safety boundary bhi hai: generative LLM ko diya gaya context sirf sabse relevant aur verified data tak narrow karke aap hallucinations aur "off-track" responses ka risk significantly kam kar dete hain. Platform dekhte waqt provider ki retrieval capabilities aur retrieval me innovate karte rehne ki commitment ko carefully dekho, aur apni team ki search technology banane aur maintain karne ki skills se compare karo.
  • Prompt engineering: DIY stack me main prompt engineering effort woh final prompt hai jo retrieved chunks ko generative LLM ko bhejte waqt use hota hai. Uske do main purposes hain: chunks ko summarize karke user query ka coherent response dena, aur careful prompt design (aur continuous updates) se prompt injection attacks se ladna aur hallucinations aur bias kam karna. Lekin saare LLMs prompts par ek jaise behave nahi karte — kuch instructions achhe se follow karte hain, kuch nahi. Prompt ko set-and-forget mat samjho — naye LLMs aate hi aur alag use cases ke liye use adapt karna pad sakta hai. RAG platform yahan strategic benefit deta hai: prompt engineering me deep expertise aur LLM-specific nuances ke saath current rehne ke alawa, platforms centralized prompt governance enable karte hain. Enterprise scale par ye alag-alag teams me inconsistent safety posture ko rokta hai aur ensure karta hai ki security protocols, hallucination checks aur bias mitigations har application par uniformly apply hon.
  • Multiple LLMs: DIY stack me aapko poora control hai ki kaunsa LLM call karna hai — commercial options (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) ya open-weight models (Llama 4, Qwen, Kimi, DeepSeek). Lekin ek subtlety hai: LLMs ki performance characteristics samay ke saath badal sakti hain — woh inputs par behave ya respond karne ka tareeka badal sakte hain. Open-weight model use karo to use GPU-equipped machines par khud host karna hoga. RAG platform provider aapka trusted partner ban jata hai — best LLM determine karna, alag LLMs test karna, unki changing characteristics track karna, aur ensure karna ki RAG application end-to-end sahi kaam kare aur generated responses ki high quality bani rahe. Kuch applications me industry-specific dataset par fine-tuned LLM beneficial ho sakta hai — DIY me use easily achieve karke fine-tuned LLM ke self-hosted version se replace kar sakte hain; platform me BYO LLM capability important hai, aur agar fine-tuned generative LLM expected hai to provider ke saath woh capability explore karo.
  • Hallucination detection aur correction: LLM ke responses me se woh identify karke correct karna jo retrieved chunks ke facts se inconsistent hon — isse response quality dramatically improve hoti hai (Chapter 3). Platform providers dekhte waqt ensure karo ki is capability ka support hai; DIY stack me in components ko implement aur samay ke saath support karne ka plan banana hoga.

Data sources aur connectors

Core capabilities ke alawa data sources aur data ingestion kaisa dikhega, ye bhi important hai. Bahut se RAG platform providers data connectors support karte hain — email systems, Google Drive, SharePoint, Notion, Jira, Confluence, web pages, internal documentation, database systems, Salesforce, ya Box ya Dropbox jaise file sources. Platform consider karte waqt connectors ko depth me explore karo: kaunse file formats supported hain? Connectors data refresh support karte hain? Error handling kaise manage hoti hai — kya connector partial failures ya data gaps (jaise skipped files) surface kar sakta hai taaki LLM incomplete knowledge base par kaam na kare? Kya connector error se gracefully recover kar sakta hai? Kya connectors granular RBAC aur real-time permission syncing support karte hain taaki data leakage na ho aur users sirf authorized information retrieve karein? Aapke IT environment me deploy karna kitna easy ya mushkil hoga? Robust aur stable data connectivity ke liye kaunsi logging aur monitoring available hai? DIY stack me external data ke liye teen options hain: connectors khud banao aur maintain karo (aur zaroorat padne par naye add karo); Airbyte jaise open source data connector project ya LlamaIndex/LangChain jaise LLM orchestration framework use karo jinme data connectors hon; ya Airbyte Cloud, LlamaCloud ya similar commercial solution use karo. Approach jo bhi ho, data sources ko hard look do aur connectors implement karne ka work effort consider karo — sirf initial ingest ke liye nahi, data refresh aur updates ke liye bhi. Open source connector projects ki tulna me LangChain ke 130+ connectors, LlamaIndex ke 160+, Airbyte aur Meltano ke 600+ connectors hain (Airbyte me built-in incremental sync, LlamaCloud me incremental updates) — lekin sirf source types ki list se aage dekhna important hai: har connector exactly kaise kaam karta hai aur kya woh aapka specific data support karta hai, ye samajhna zaroori hai. Example: ek email connector Gmail ke saath kaam kare lekin Outlook ke saath nahi; ek HubSpot connector CRM ka sirf hissa import kare; ek Jira connector sirf tickets import kare, unke attachments nahi.

RAG sprawl aur centralized governance

DIY RAG full granular control deta hai, lekin isse RAG sprawl ho sakta hai — organization bhar me alag-alag, independently managed RAG applications ka proliferation. Har application ka apna vector database, embedding model aur generative LLM ho sakta hai, aur data ingest process ki alag implementations. Ye central IT ke liye nightmare ban jata hai — multiple tarah ke RAG components manage karne hote hain, har ek apni complexity ke saath, aur bahut se organizational policies se incompatible ho sakte hain. Security ke angle se har DIY application ke apne access controls, data handling policies aur security configurations ho sakte hain — consistent security measures enforce karna aur vulnerabilities effectively monitor karna challenging ho jata hai. Is fragmentation se "policy drift" hoti hai — security aur compliance guarantees samay ke saath erode ho jati hain jab individual pipelines centralized oversight ke bina update ya modify hoti hain. Standardization ki kami se (anajane me) alag-alag protection levels wale data silos ban sakte hain, data breaches, unauthorized access aur GDPR ya California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) jaise regulations ke saath compliance failures ka risk badh jata hai. Yahan RAG platform shine karta hai — centralized aur standardized approach deta hai: IT resources (storage aur compute, CPUs aur GPUs) manage karna, data governance, observability, auditability aur release processes ke liye built-in mechanisms, aur robust access control, encryption protocols aur audit trails jaise security features. Isse IT policies consistently saari RAG applications par apply hoti hain aur RAG sprawl avoid hota hai. Example: marketing department ek RAG application banati hai, anajane me noncompliant vector database use karke EU customer data bina proper GDPR masking ke ingest kar deti hai; usi samay legal team contract review ke liye alag, highly secure LLM se dusra RAG system banati hai. Central IT ko marketing app ke compliance risk ki visibility hi nahi hai, aur ek single data handling standard enforce karne ka tareeka bhi nahi. RAG platform ek single, pre-configured "golden path" dekar solve karta hai: approved vector store use karna enforce karta hai aur saari nayi applications par automatically PII redaction rules apply karta hai, chahe koi bhi department banaye. Centralization resource duplication bhi rokti hai aur costs kat-ti hai — sprawl environment me data science team ek bade, expensive embedding model ko ek project ke liye deploy kar sakti hai, aur sales team anjaane me wahi model wahi data par apne chatbot ke liye dobara deploy kar de — ingestion costs double. Ye duplication data se aage jati hai: dono teams alag storage ke liye pay kar rahi hain, high-demand GPU/CPU resources use kar rahi hain, aur upgrade aur maintenance ke liye alag engineering aur DevOps teams bandhi hui hain. Security ke angle se consolidation critical hai: sprawl me har RAG application alag, isolated target ban jati hai jise independently secure, monitor aur patch karna hota hai — vulnerability scanner ko legal team ki nayi RAG app ke baare me pata bhi nahi ho sakta. Platform-based approach ek single, hardened perimeter deta hai — consistent RBAC, uniform encryption standards, aur saari RAG applications par ek saath comprehensive vulnerability tests. Shared component me nayi vulnerability mile to ek baar platform level par patch karo, aur use karne wali har application turant protected ho jati hai. Companies aaj "shadow IT" (IT ya security group ki knowledge ke bina department ya individual dwara IT hardware/software ka use) se bachne ki koshish karti hain, aur ab uske naye incarnation "shadow AI" se aur zyada mehnat se bach rahi hain — kyunki shadow AI ke cost, compliance aur security risks orders of magnitude zyada hain.

Cost aur upkeep — DIY dikhne me sasta, asal me mehenga

DIY approach aksar RAG journey ka pehla step hota hai — teams generative AI seekhti hain aur pehle prototypes banakar organization ko value demonstrate karti hain. DIY aksar sasta dikhta hai agar sirf direct subscription fees dekho — LLMs use karne ki token costs. Lekin direct API use costs bhi jaldi balloon kar sakti hain agar API usage ko carefully monitor aur control na karo aur continuously optimize na karo. RAG ki true costs usse bahut zyada hain: underlying infrastructure (vector databases, LLMs, embedding models, rerankers) ka setup, configuration aur ongoing maintenance; har RAG component ki research, design aur testing me extensive time; aur infrastructure maintain karne, security vulnerabilities patch karne, models aur algorithms update karne, prompt re-engineering, retrieval pipeline improve karne, hallucination mitigation controls aur usage badhne par infrastructure scale karne ka continuous operational burden. Ye responsibilities specialized skills wali dedicated team mangti hain — persistent operational expenditure aur internal resources ka drain, jo core business innovation par focus kar sakte the. Iske contrast me RAG platform ongoing maintenance aur operational overhead ka zyadaatar hissa vendor par shift kar deta hai, high aur unpredictable TCO ko zyada predictable TCO se replace karne me madad karta hai — aksar do distinct pricing models me se ek me: developer-centric consumption model — bottoms-up adoption ke liye, free tiers aur kam initial monthly subscriptions ($50–$500) jinme base set of resources shamil hai; TCO variable rehta hai kyunki costs granular pay-as-you-go overages se drive hoti hain (examples: Ragie.ai aur LlamaCloud); all-in-one enterprise model — bade enterprises ke liye, TCO predictability ke liye priced (Vectara ek example hai) — aksar annual subscription jisme "credits" ka bada annual bundle shamil hota hai, ek abstract unit of value jo saari underlying costs (API calls, data storage, compute, retrieval) ko ek single, predictable metric me bundle kar deta hai. Pricing consumption-based ho ya annual subscription, fees me updates, security aur platform evolution cover hote hain. Vendors incentivized hote hain apne platforms ko cutting edge par rakhne ke liye — latest LLMs, retrieval techniques aur security practices incorporate karte hue — taaki customers apne specific RAG use cases par focus kar sakein.

Deployment options — SaaS, VPC, on-premises

Deployment option chunte waqt yaad rakho ki SaaS solution, zyada customizable VPC deployment ya fully self-managed on-premises setup ka choice control ke level, support SLAs, areas of responsibility aur resource allocation par implications rakhta hai. DIY RAG me flexibility bahut hai — lagbhag kahin bhi deploy kar sakte hain; limitations components se aati hain. Example: vector database managed service hai aur on-premises RAG system chahiye to alag vector database chunni hogi aur locally deploy karni hogi; on-premises environment me data bahar jaane se rokne wali policy ke karan commercial API-based LLM, embedding model ya reranker use nahi kar sakte, self-hosted LLM par bharosa karna hoga. RAG platform vendors me zyadaatar sirf SaaS deployment option support karte hain — vendor poora stack manage karta hai aur hyperscaler provider ko infrastructure costs directly pay karta hai — halanki kuch VPC aur on-premises options bhi support karte hain. SaaS model me bahut se providers ensure karte hain ki adequate security aur data governance controls hon, taaki SaaS offering HIPAA, GDPR ya SOC-2 comply kare. Lekin organization ko apne data aur environment par zyada control chahiye ho, ya "air-gapped" installation chahiye ho jahan koi data systems se bahar na jaye, to SaaS approach bilkul nonstarter hai. VPC deployment (AWS, Azure ya Google Cloud ke VPC me) RAG application ko cloud ke isolated segment me chalata hai — network security aur data privacy par zyada granular control; is model me team se zyada cloud architecture aur MLOps expertise chahiye hoti hai, aur ye un businesses ko suit karta hai jo pehle se dusri cloud-based applications implement karte hain ya jinki compliance requirements controlled cloud environment me meet ho sakti hain. On-premises deployment highest level of control deta hai, aur greatest responsibility bhi: poora RAG stack organization ke apne data centers me host karna ensure karta hai ki data kabhi company ke physical perimeter se bahar na jaye — highly sensitive data wali companies (financial services ya healthcare), stringent regulatory obligations, ya air-gapped environments ke liye favored. Lekin isme specific architectural challenges hain: hardware infrastructure (CAPEX vs OPEX — API costs ke badle significant upfront hardware investment; high-performance RAG ke liye enterprise-grade GPUs jaise Nvidia A100/H100 chahiye, jinme LLM weights memory me hold karne ke liye kaafi VRAM ho), local model inference (air-gapped environment me external APIs call nahi kar sakte, isliye commercial LLMs nahi use kar sakte — open-weight ya self-hosted models (jaise Llama 4, Mistral, DeepSeek, gpt-oss) par bharosa karna hoga aur local inference servers manage karne honge; sirf LLM hi nahi, standard ingestion pipelines bhi aksar cloud-based OCR ya parsing APIs par bharosa karti hain, aur on-premises setup me har step ke liye local alternatives deploy karne honge — embedding models, rerankers aur images ya tables ke liye multimodal processing tools), aur operational overhead (infrastructure manage karna, OS security vulnerabilities patch karna, model weights manually update karna, container orchestration (aksar Kubernetes ke through) manage karna, aur saare systems ki logging aur monitoring). Aakhir me SaaS, VPC aur on-premises ke beech decision organization ki priorities par depend karta hai — data security, control, customization needs, available technical expertise, budget aur desired speed of deployment. Koi one-size-fits-all answer nahi hai: SaaS ease aur speed ko prioritize karta hai, on-premises control aur data isolation ko, aur VPC flexible middle ground deta hai.

Yaad rakho: Platform chunne se pehle har capability ko alag se check karo — embedding BYO, retrieval quality, connectors, RBAC sync, deployment options. Aur yaad rakho: DIY me sprawl sabse bada chhupa hua risk hai — ek golden path ke bina har team apna alag RAG bana legi, aur central IT ko pata bhi nahi chalega.
SOURCESource: Hands-On RAG for Production, O'Reilly, Chapter 5 — The RAG Platform

05.2Chapter 5 · The RAG Platform

Example RAG Platform: Vectara

DIY approach me har component pick aur integrate karna hota hai — open source (jaise LlamaIndex, LangChain, Weaviate) ya managed services (jaise Cohere, Pinecone, Gemini, OpenAI). Major cloud providers middle ground dete hain, lekin true end-to-end RAG platforms (jaise Vectara ya Nuclia) saare components — document extraction, chunking, embedding, vector storage, retrieval, generation aur hallucination detection — ko ek single, unified API me bundle kar dete hain. Is section me Vectara ko example platform ke roop me dekhte hain, taaki samajh aaye ki ek standardized API data ingestion, query parametrization aur hallucination mitigation ko kaise control karti hai aur RAG sprawl ko kaise rokti hai.

Getting started — account, Console aur corpus

Vectara se shuru karne ke liye pehle account banao, phir Console use karo — ye web-based interface hai jisse aap apna Vectara account, corpora aur data manage karte hain. Vectara me corpus ka matlab hai saare ingested data ka virtual container, jo query karne ke liye pre-process, clean aur organize kiya gaya hai. Har corpus isolated hota hai, taaki alag applications ke liye distinct datasets rakh sakein — example: ek corpus company ki internal documentation ke liye, dusra customer support tickets ke liye, teesra product reviews ke liye. Documents corpus ke andar information ke individual pieces hain, jo baad me search aur responses generate karne ke liye use hote hain. Corpus banane ke steps: "Corpora" section me jao, "Create corpus" click karo, aur ye details do — name (corpus ke liye user-friendly naam), key (corpus key — API requests me use hone wala unique corpus identifier), description (optional — content ya purpose explain karne wala text), embedding model (data vectorize karne ka model — yahan Vectara ka built-in embedding model "Boomerang" chunna hai), aur filter attributes (optional lekin recommended — filtering ke liye use hone wale metadata fields define karo: attribute name, uska data type — text, integer, boolean, real — aur kya woh document level (doc) par apply hota hai ya document-part level (part) par; ye bhi chun sakte hain ki use faster filtering ke liye index karna hai ya nahi). Corpus banne ke baad woh data receive karne ke liye ready hai.

API keys — teen types

Corpus ke saath API se kaam karne se pehle Vectara API key banani hoti hai. Teen types hain: personal API key (aapke Vectara account par kisi bhi API operation ke liye full permissions), query-only API key (naam se hi clear — sirf corpus ko query karne ki access), aur query+index API key (data index karne — directly ya file upload se — aur corpus query karne dono ki permissions). Neeche ke examples me corpus key "RAGBOOK" use hoti hai, aur assume kiya gaya hai ki aapne query+index API key ya personal API key banayi hai. Vectara OAuth 2.0 ke through bhi saari API functionality ki access support karta hai (API key ke bajaye), lekin woh is book ke scope se bahar hai.

Ingesting data — file upload

Corpus ready hone ke baad data upload aur index karne ke options dekhte hain. File upload se aap alag-alag types ki files (jaise PDF, Word, PPT, HTML, Markdown ya text) upload_file endpoint se Vectara me upload kar sakte hain. API response upload operation ke baare me useful information deta hai — file ki id, metadata (jaise producer aur title) aur storage usage (kitne bytes use hue). Peeche kya hota hai: pehle Vectara file content receive karta hai — PDF file ho to usse actual text extract karta hai; phir text ko Vectara ki default chunking strategy ("sentence chunking") se chunk kiya jata hai; phir Boomerang embedding model har chunk par apply hota hai, resulting vector embeddings Vectara ke internal vector database me store hote hain, aur har chunk ka text (metadata ke saath, agar available ho) vector embedding ke saath ek alag text database me store hota hai. Ye process platform ki abstraction dikhata hai: text extraction, multimodal processing, chunking, embedding aur vector store ka management — saari complexity platform handle karta hai. File upload ke saath optional arguments se additional capabilities chun sakte hain: file par apply karne wali chunking strategy select karna (sentence ya fixed chunking), file par table extraction ya image extraction enable karna (taaki uploaded document me embedded tables ya images RAG pipeline me sahi se handle hon), aur document ko metadata fields attach karna (jaise PDF document me author name ya creation date). API call parameters configure karke ingestion process customize karne ki ye ability hi batati hai ki RAG platform me kya hota hai: bahut si capabilities pehle se platform me hain, aur aap API call parameters configure karke chunte hain ki kaunsi chahiye — DIY ke contrast me, jahan har capability khud banani aur maintain karni hoti hai.

Ingesting data — direct data ingestion

File upload ke alawa aap text data directly bhi Vectara me ingest kar sakte hain. Ye un data ke liye useful hai jo individual files se originate nahi karta, balki database ya dusre sources (jaise Notion, Jira, Confluence, Salesforce ya Slack) se aata hai. Direct ingestion me aap document ko structured form me bhejte hain — document-level id, type, title aur metadata ke saath, aur text ko sections me tod kar. Sections nested bhi ho sakte hain, taaki data source me text ki complex representations support hon, aur har section par metadata bhi add kar sakte hain. Response me document ki id, metadata aur storage usage milta hai. Ab corpus me data hai, to dekhte hain ki API se queries kaise execute karte hain.

Running queries — ek API call me poora flow

Query flow (Chapter 1 wala) me query full retrieval pipeline se guzarti hai — vector search, hybrid search aur reranking ho sakta hai; phir retrieved chunks ko context ke roop me include karke prompt craft kiya jata hai aur generative LLM ko call karke response generate kiya jata hai; aur final step hai hallucination detection aur correction. RAG platform API query process ko simplify karke aksar ek single API call me kar deta hai. Vectara me query call me ye parameters hote hain: search section me lexical_interpolation (hybrid search enabled hai ya nahi, aur interpolation value kya hai), offset aur limit (kitne results), context_configuration (har chunk ke aas-paas kitne sentences pehle aur baad me include karne hain — jaise 2 sentences before aur 2 after), aur reranker (kaunsa reranker use karna hai, jaise multilingual reranker); generation section me max_used_search_results (generative LLM ko kitne search results/chunks bhejne hain, jaise 7), response_language (jaise "eng"), prompt_name (generation preset — jo generative LLM aur prompt determine karta hai), aur enable_factual_consistency_score (factual consistency score enable karna). Response me summary milta hai, saath me factual consistency score (hallucination score) — book ke example me pet policy wali query par summary aata hai aur factual consistency score 0.77734375 milta hai — aur search_results me retrieved chunks ka poora set bhi milta hai. Query API bahut detail chhupane ke baad bhi kaafi flexibility aur control deti hai: hybrid search ka interpolation, reranker ka choice, generation preset (LLM aur prompt), aur LLM ko bheje jaane wale search results ki sankhya. Ek aur argument hai stream_response — jab true set ho to Vectara response ko ek single text string ke roop me bhejne ke bajaye "streaming" karta hai, taaki application ka user interface query response ko word by word display kar sake, final response ka wait kiye bina.

Hallucination correction — correct_hallucinations endpoint

Query call factual consistency score ke saath hallucinated ho sakne wale responses detect karne me madad karta hai. Correction ke liye Vectara ka correct_hallucinations API endpoint hai. Isme aap generated text aur retrieved documents ka text bhejte hain, aur ek correction model (jaise vhc-large-1.0) specify karte hain. Response me corrected text milta hai — book ke example me hallucinated response me do galat facts the (birds ke liye "no rules" aur banned pets me "snakes") — corrected text me dono sahi ho jate hain (birds ke liye specific guidelines hain, aur cats aur dogs allowed nahi hain). Aap actual corrections bhi display kar sakte hain: har correction me original text, corrected text aur explanation hota hai — kaunsa span galat tha, kya correction hua, aur kyun (source kya kehta hai). Ye breakdown useful hai kyunki ye dikhata hai ki exactly kis span me kya correction hua aur uske peeche reasoning kya hai.

Other RAG Admin API endpoints

Ingest/upload aur query sabse zyada use hone wale endpoints hain, lekin Vectara me administration ke liye aur bhi bahut se API endpoints hain: corpora (saare corpora list karo, corpus create karo, corpus delete karo), documents (saare documents list karo, document delete karo, document ka full text ya summary retrieve karo), API keys (API keys list karo, create aur delete karo), user management (account par user create karo aur unki permissions specify karo, saare users list karo, user delete karo, user ka password reset karo), aur query history (query history aur account se judi additional analytics dekho). Example: corpus ke saare documents list karne par do documents dikhte hain — file upload se ingested pet policy document aur direct ingestion se ingested structured document — har ek apni metadata ke saath. RAG platform chunte waqt ensure karna important hai ki us platform me similar API endpoints hon, taaki administrative tasks automate ho sakein. Isse central IT multiple RAG applications ko behtar manage kar sakta hai, ingest aur query activity samajh sakta hai, users ke join aur leave karne par manage kar sakta hai, aur organization ki saari RAG applications me important IT tasks automate kar sakta hai.

Yaad rakho: Platform ki asli taakat ek API call me poora RAG flow chhupana hai — lekin control khatm nahi hota. Reranker, hybrid interpolation, generation preset aur factual consistency score jaise parameters se aap abhi bhi retrieval aur generation ko tune kar sakte hain — bas infrastructure aapko maintain nahi karna padta.
vectara-ingest.ipynb — Ingest Data into Vectara — GitHub: ofermend/hands-on-rag, chapter5/vectara-ingest.ipynb (https://github.com/ofermend/hands-on-rag/blob/main/chapter5/vectara-ingest.ipynb)
import requests
import json
import os

CORPUS_KEY = "RAGBOOK"
VECTARA_API_KEY = os.getenv("VECTARA_API_KEY")

# Create corpus if it doesn't exist
headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
    "x-api-key": VECTARA_API_KEY
}

create_corpus_payload = {
    "key": CORPUS_KEY,
    "name": "RAG Book Examples",
    "description": "Corpus for Hands-on RAG book examples"
}

response = requests.post("https://api.vectara.io/v2/corpora", headers=headers, json=create_corpus_payload)
if response.status_code == 201:
    print(f"Created corpus '{CORPUS_KEY}'")
elif response.status_code == 409:
    print(f"Corpus '{CORPUS_KEY}' already exists")
else:
    print(f"Create corpus returned: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")

url = f"https://api.vectara.io/v2/corpora/{CORPUS_KEY}/upload_file"

payload={}
files=[
  ('file',
  ( 'pet_policy',
    open('pet_policy.pdf','rb'),
    'application/octet-stream')
  )
]
headers = {
  'Accept': 'application/json',
  'x-api-key': VECTARA_API_KEY
}

response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, data=payload, files=files)
res = response.json()
print(f"Upload status: {response.status_code}")
print(res)

url = f"https://api.vectara.io/v2/corpora/{CORPUS_KEY}/documents"

payload = json.dumps({
  "id": "selected-works-of-shakespeare",
  "type": "structured",
  "title": "William Shakespeare, Greatest Hits",
  "metadata": {
    "timespan": "26 April 1564---23 April 1616",
    "stars": 5,
    "author": "William Shakespeare"
  },
  "sections": [
    {
      "title": "King Lear",
      "text": "Synopsis: King Lear, intending to divide his power and kingdom among his three daughters, demands public professions of their love. His youngest daughter, ...",
      "sections": [
        {
          "title": "Act I",
          "text": "KENT: I thought the king had more affected the Duke of Albany than Cornwall.\nGLOUCESTER: It did always seem so to us...",
          "metadata": {
            "stage-instructions": "Enter KENT, GLOUCESTER, and EDMUND"
          }
        },
        {
          "title": "Act II",
          "text": "EDMUND: Save thee, Curan. ...",
          "metadata": {
            "stage-instructions": "Enter EDMUND, and CURAN meets him"
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "title": "Antony and Cleopatra",
      "text": "PHILO: Nay, but this dotage of our general's\nO'erflows the measure: those his goodly eyes, ..."
    }
  ]
})

headers = {
  'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  'Accept': 'application/json',
  'x-api-key': VECTARA_API_KEY
}

response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, data=payload)
res = response.json()
print(f"Index document status: {response.status_code}")
print(res)

import requests
import json
import os

CORPUS_KEY = "RAGBOOK"
VECTARA_API_KEY = os.getenv("VECTARA_API_KEY")

url = f"https://api.vectara.io/v2/corpora/{CORPUS_KEY}/query"
query_str = "Are pets allowed in the office?"

payload = json.dumps({
  "query": query_str,
  "search": {
    "lexical_interpolation": 0.025,
    "offset": 0,
    "limit": 50,
    "context_configuration": {
      "sentences_before": 2,
      "sentences_after": 2
    },
    "reranker": {
      "type": "customer_reranker",
      "reranker_name": "Rerank_Multilingual_v1"
    }
  },
  "generation": {
    "max_used_search_results": 7,
    "response_language": "eng",
    "generation_preset_name": "vectara-summary-ext-24-05-med-omni",
    "enable_factual_consistency_score": True
  }
})
headers = {
  'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  'Accept': 'application/json',
  'x-api-key': VECTARA_API_KEY
}

response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, data=payload)
res = response.json()
search_results = res['search_results']

print(res['summary'])
print(f"Factual Consistency Score: {res['factual_consistency_score']}")

search_results[:2]

hallucinated_response = """
Pets are allowed in the office at Vectara, but with specific guidelines. 
Birds are permitted and even encouraged in the workspace, but there are no rules to follow [2]. 
However, common household pets like cats and snakes are not allowed on the Vectara campuses [7].
"""

url = f"https://api.vectara.io/v2/hallucination_correctors/correct_hallucinations"
payload = {
  "generated_text": hallucinated_response,
  "query": query_str,
  "documents": [
      {"text": r["text"]}
      for r in search_results
  ],
  "model_name": "vhc-large-1.0"
}
headers = {
  'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  'Accept': 'application/json',
  'x-api-key': VECTARA_API_KEY
}

response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload)
res = response.json()

print("Original (hallucinated):")
print(hallucinated_response)
print("\nCorrected:")
print(res['corrected_text'])

res['corrections']

06Chapter 6 · Evaluating Your RAG Application

Evaluating Your RAG Application — How Does RAG Fail?

Chahe aap DIY RAG banayein ya RAG platform use karein, aapko ye measure karna hi hoga ki users ko dikhne wale responses ki quality kaisi hai. Ise RAG evaluation kehte hain — ye measure karta hai ki system sahi documents ya chunks kitni accurately dhoondhta hai (retrieval accuracy) aur un documents ya chunks se response kitni coherently aur correctly craft karta hai (generation accuracy). Evaluation ke do types hain: offline evaluation — development cycle ke dauraan ki jati hai, deep aur aksar resource-heavy, pipeline settings ko deployment se pehle optimize karne ke liye; aur online evaluation — live traffic par ki jati hai, real users system se kaise interact karte hain ye identify karti hai, lekin low-latency user experience banaye rakhne ke liye lightweight approach chahiye hoti hai. Ye chapter primarily offline RAG evaluation par focus karta hai — ye kyun important hai, kaunse metrics consider karne chahiye, aur har metric ko kaise interpret karna hai.

Evaluation na karna business risk hai

RAG application ki quality measure karne ka systematic approach na hona sirf technical oversight nahi hai — ye business risk hai jo aapki poori AI strategy ko undermine kar sakta hai. Bina structured, rigorous evaluation framework ke aap aisi applications deploy karne ka risk lete hain jo hallucinations ya inaccurate answers deti hain, aur aakhir me user trust erode kar deti hain aur business ko milne wale benefits degrade kar deti hain. Production me ye technical failures lower customer satisfaction (jo lower customer satisfaction scores se indicate ho sakta hai), lower net promoter scores (NPS), ya costly compliance incidents ke rise ke roop me manifest hote hain. RAG query flow kam se kam do distinct lekin interdependent components se banta hai — retriever aur generator. Query flow ke kisi bhi component me failure ya degradation poor-quality outputs de sakta hai. Isliye robust evaluation strategy ko query flow ke saare components ko independently diagnose karne me capable hona chahiye, saath me unki synergistic performance assess karni chahiye. In technical components ko retrieval aur generation ke evaluation metrics aur system metrics (latency aur uptime) se link karke aap ensure kar sakte hain ki aapka RAG stack measurable business outcomes ke liye optimized hai.

Retrieval failures — low recall aur low precision

RAG me sabse critical aur common failures me se ek retrieval ke dauraan hota hai — aur jab retrieval process flawed ho to poora system compromised ho jata hai. Generator LLM kitna bhi advanced kyun na ho, woh incorrect ya irrelevant context se correct, relevant answer produce nahi kar sakta. Production me recommendation hai ki generative LLM se pehle retriever ko optimize karo — basic vector search se hybrid search (vector search + BM25) par switch karna ya reranker add karna measurable gains de sakta hai. Agar retrieval recall 40% hai to koi bhi prompt engineering aapki RAG application ko successful nahi bana sakti. Retrieval me do common failure modes hain: failure to retrieve (low recall) — dataset me user query ka jawab dene ke liye exact information hai, lekin retrieval mechanism use surface karne me poori tarah fail ho jata hai. Isse LLM effectively blind ho jata hai — complete failure (retriever ko koi relevant information hi nahi milti, LLM ke paas response ground karne ke liye kuch nahi hota) ya partial failure (system kuch relevant chunks retrieve karta hai lekin comprehensive aur accurate answer ke liye zaroori dusre critical pieces miss kar deta hai). In scenarios me LLM corner me phas jata hai: ya to admit kare ki use information nahi mili (jo aksar unhelpful hota hai), ya — zyada dangerously — apne pre-trained knowledge par fallback karke plausible-sounding lekin fabricated ya outdated response hallucinate kar de. Irrelevant retrieval (low precision) — retriever "noisy" hota hai: document chunks successfully dhoondhta hai, lekin unme se kuch ya saare user query ke liye relevant nahi hote aur query ka jawab dene ke liye zaroori specific facts nahi rakhte. Example: user poochta hai ki naye repository ke liye kaunse security protocols required hain, aur retriever general information wale chunks pull kar leta hai jo topic se related to hain lekin specific sawaal ka jawab dene ke liye useless hain. Book ek example deti hai: query hai project launch ka mandatory final approval step aur risk assessment form submit karne ki specific deadline. System ke paas teen chunks hain — Chunk A (relevant: final mandatory step "Stakeholder Sign-off" hai), Chunk B (relevant: risk assessment forms launch se 72 hours pehle Compliance Portal par submit karne hain), Chunk C (irrelevant/noisy: launch ke baad team celebration lunch ke liye budget use karne ki salah). Retriever Chunk A identify karta hai lekin Chunk B retrieve karne me fail ho jata hai, aur uske bajaye Chunk C pull kar leta hai kyunki usme "Project" aur "launch" words hain. LLM ab sirf Stakeholder Sign-off aur team celebration ki jaankari se jawab banata hai — deadline ke baare me kehta hai ki documentation me timeframe specify nahi hai, aur celebration lunch ka noisy distraction add kar deta hai. User assume kar sakta hai ki koi deadline hai hi nahi, jisse compliance window miss ho sakti hai aur project launch delay ho sakta hai. Robust retrieval ke liye precision aur recall dono ko simultaneously optimize karna hota hai — recall@k, precision@k, nDCG ya UMBRELA jaise metrics se retrieval pipeline ke issues identify aur fix kar sakte hain, taaki generative LLM ke paas sahi facts hon.

Retrieval ki architectural limits

Kai retrieval failures pipeline ko tune karke fix kiye ja sakte hain, lekin kuch failures retrieval method ki architectural limits me rooted hote hain. Standard RAG complex, multi-hop queries (jaise "us company ka HQ kahan hai jisne Startup X ko acquire kiya?") ya broad "sensemaking" queries (jaise "engineering team nayi policy ke baare me kya sochti hai?") ke saath struggle karta hai. In queries ko simple semantic matching se zyada chahiye hota hai, aur inhe solve karne ke liye agentic RAG (Chapter 7) ya knowledge graphs (Chapter 9) ki taraf dekhna hota hai.

Generation failures — faithfulness, context utilization, answer relevance

Retrieval perfectly (ya kam se kam reasonably achhe se) kaam kare — best chunks mil jayein — tab bhi generation step me failures ki wajah se poor results aa sakte hain. Effective RAG system ko sirf retriever me achha librarian nahi chahiye, generator me competent aur trustworthy author bhi chahiye. Generation failures ke teen important types hain: faithfulness failure — sabse commonly hallucination ke naam se jana jata hai, aur arguably sabse severe generation error hai — jab LLM ka answer provided chunks me diye gaye facts ko directly contradict karta hai ya unse supported nahi hota. Example: ek chunk explicitly kehta hai project deadline July 31st hai, aur LLM confidently jawab deta hai ki deadline early August me hai — usne apni primary directive fail ki hai ki response provided information me grounded ho. Enterprise users ke liye jo factual accuracy par bharosa karte hain, ye sabse destructive error ho sakta hai, kyunki ye application ki credibility ko poori tarah tod deta hai. Yahan do cheezein distinguish karna helpful hai: faithful incorrectness (LLM ne response sirf provided chunks me ground kiya, lekin provided information hi galat thi) vs unfaithful incorrectness (final answer source data me reflect nahi hota). Ek response outdated document ke prati perfectly faithful ho sakta hai — example: stale PDF document me mili 2023 ki deadline ko accurately state karna — phir bhi user ke liye 2024 me incorrect ho sakta hai. Inhe distinguish karna troubleshooting ke liye vital hai: agar response unfaithful hai to LLM at fault ho sakta hai, lekin agar faithful lekin incorrect hai to retriever ne outdated chunks fetch kiye hain, aur data ingestion pipeline fix karni hogi ya document versioning implement karni hogi. Context utilization failure — retriever ne multiple relevant chunks successfully identify aur provide kiye, lekin LLM un sab ko final answer me incorporate karne me fail ho jata hai. Ye LLM challenges jaise ordering bias (sirf pehle ya aakhri chunk par focus karna) ki wajah se ho sakta hai, jahan model provided context ke crucial pieces ko effectively ignore kar deta hai. Example: user poochta hai ek project ke financial risks aur benefits kya hain; retriever do chunks deta hai — ek revenue potential (benefits) ke baare me, dusra market volatility (risks) ke baare me. Agar LLM sirf revenue benefits describe kare aur risks wale context ko poori tarah ignore kar de to ye context utilization failure hai. Resulting answer hallucination nahi hai, kyunki woh kuch context me grounded hai, lekin dangerously incomplete aur misleading hai — skewed picture dekar poor decision making ki taraf le ja sakta hai. AutoNuggetizer (generation metrics me aage) context utilization me gaps identify karne ka ek approach hai. Answer relevance failure — LLM ka answer provided context ke prati poori tarah faithful ho sakta hai aur saare relevant facts include kar sakta hai, lekin aakhir me user ke core question ya intent ko address karne me fail ho jata hai. Example: user poochta hai "kya naya update push karna safe hai?" aur context update ke features list karta hai — to "naye update me features A, B aur C hain" jaisa answer factually correct hai, lekin inference ka bojh user par wapas daal deta hai, jise features interpret karke decide karna hoga ki update safe hai ya nahi. System requested conclusive insight dene me fail ho jata hai. Answer similarity metrics jaise ROUGE-L aur BERTScore (generated answer ko "ground truth" answer se compare karte hain) is tarah ki failure ko miss kar dete hain, isliye effective nahi hain — custom rubric ke saath LLM-as-a-judge aksar behtar perform karta hai.

Failures due to inadequate data ingestion

"Garbage in, garbage out" ka principle RAG par acutely relevant hai. System ke output ki quality fundamentally ingested data ki quality se limited hoti hai. Agar ingestion pipeline — source documents ko parse, clean aur index karne ka process — flawed hai, to woh data jiss par RAG grounded hona chahiye, essentially compromised hai. Retriever kitna bhi accurate ho ya generator kitna bhi precise ho, woh incomplete, improperly structured, obsolete ya simply galat source of truth ko compensate nahi kar sakte. Data ingestion me do common challenges hain: structural parsing error — ingestion process complex document formats ko sahi se interpret karne me fail ho jata hai, ya PDF, DOCX ya PPTX documents ke andar tables, charts ya images se relevant information properly extract nahi kar pata. Text extract ho sakta hai, lekin uska tabular ya hierarchical context kho jata hai, structured data ko words ki meaningless sequence me badal deta hai. Ye aksar table-heavy ya highly visual documents par systematically low retrieval relevance ke roop me manifest hota hai. Ingestion pipeline me robust logging implement karne se is tarah ki failures proactively identify aur fix ki ja sakti hain. Content staleness — data ingestion pipeline regularly data refresh bhi kare to bhi outdated ya superseded documents sahi se remove ya version nahi hote. RAG application phir ek saal purane policy document se "confidently" information retrieve karke use current fact ke roop me present kar sakti hai, jisse users dangerously obsolete information par act kar sakte hain. Content staleness address karne ka sabse straightforward tareeka hai har document ke liye unique entity ID aur versioning: saare documents aur unke chunks ko entity ID aur version number se mark karo; jab us document ka naya version ingest ho to previous versions ke saare chunks remove kar do. Iske saath stale data ke liye proactive tests bhi chala sakte hain — agar ek hi document (entity ID) ke do versions system me present hain to kuch galat hai ingestion process me.

Summary of RAG failures

Aakhir me, inadequate ingestion indirectly retrieval aur generation failures trigger karta hai. Ye ingestion-related issues khaas taur par insidious hain kyunki ye false sense of reliability banate hain — system perfectly function karta hua dikh sakta hai, phir bhi flawed foundation par operate kar raha hota hai. Book ki summary table ke hisaab se: retrieval me failure to retrieve (low recall) — hybrid search ya reranker se fix karo; irrelevant retrieval (low precision) — hybrid search ya reranker se fix karo; architectural limits — agentic RAG ya knowledge graphs par transition karo. Generation me hallucination — hallucination detection mechanism use karo; context utilization failure — prompt engineering optimize karo taaki saare chunks weighted hon; answer relevance failure — custom LLM-as-a-judge rubric implement karo. Ingestion me structural parsing error — pipeline me robust logging aur PDF/DOCX/PPTX ke liye specialized parsers use karo; content staleness — unique entity IDs aur versioning use karo. Failure modes samajhne ke baad ab metrics dekhte hain jo in failures ko identify karne me madad karte hain — lekin metrics me dive karne se pehle ek common aur critical technique samajhni hogi jo kai RAG evaluation metrics me use hoti hai: LLM-as-a-judge.

Yaad rakho: Retrieval pehle fix karo, generator baad me. Agar retriever sahi chunks hi nahi la raha to best LLM bhi sahi jawab nahi de sakta — aur agar data hi purana ya galat parse hua hai to retriever aur generator dono bekaar hain.
